SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r1.claim: إن is conditional and governs the clause لم تفعلوا; لم makes تفعلوا jussive, and the whole negative clause occupies the conditional's jussive position.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r1.anchor: " إن " الشرطية داخلة على جملة " لم تفعلوا " وتفعلوا مجزوم بلم

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r2.claim: فاتقوا is the conditional apodosis; ولن تفعلوا is parenthetical between the condition and its answer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r2.anchor: وقوله: " فاتقوا " جواب الشرط، ويكون قوله: " ولن تفعلوا " جملة معترضة بين الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r3.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r3.claim: They understand the challenge as: summon your supporters if truthful, and you will not do so; if you fail, fear the Fire. The author objects to this account.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r3.anchor: وقال جماعة من المفسرين: معنى الآية: وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r4.claim: The generic فعلوا stands in for producing a surah: فعل is a broad circumlocution that avoids spelling out the full action.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r4.anchor: فعبر بالفعل عن الإتيان لأن الفعل يجري مجرى الكناية، فيعبر به عن كل فعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says فعلوا replaces أتوا to avoid repeating the longer phrase أتوا بسورة من مثله twice.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " لو لم يعدل من لفظ الإتيان إلى لفظ الفعل لاستطيل أن يقال

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r6.claim: The Sheikh replies that فإن لم تأتوا ولن تأتوا would convey the same sense concisely by omitting the object, as with تفعلوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يلزم ما قال لأنه لو قال: " فإن لم تأتوا ولن تأتوا " كان المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r7.claim: لن governs the subjunctive imperfect and negates the future, but does not make the negation permanent or indicate a shorter span than لا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r7.anchor: " لن " حرف نصب معناه نفي المستقبل، ويختص بصيغة المضارع ك " لم " ، ولا يقتضي نفيه التأبيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r8.speaker: الخليل
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r8.claim: Al-Khalil's analysis derives لن from لا أن; the author rejects this, along with the claims that its ن replaces the alif of لا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r8.anchor: ولا نونه بدلا من ألف لا، ولا هو مركبا من " لا أن " خلافا للخليل

SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda and others allow لن to govern the jussive, citing poetry; the author says the examples can instead be explained as poetic sukūn, including al-Nabigha's line.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24/r9.anchor: وزعم قوم أنها قد تجزم، منهم أبو عبيدة وأنشدوا: 277 لن يخب لان من رجائك

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r1.claim: The common form is اتقى يتقي; Tamim and Asad also use تقى يتقي, with a variation that vocalizes the consonant after the imperfect prefix.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r1.anchor: والكثير في لغة العرب: " اتقى يتقي " على افتعل يفتعل، ولغة تميم وأسد: تقى يتقي

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r2.claim: Sibawayh records تقى يتقي with the letter after the imperfect prefix quiescent; some speakers instead vocalize it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r2.anchor: مثل: رمى يرمي، فيسكنون ما بعد حرف المضارعة، حكى هذه اللغة سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r3.claim: Poetry attests تقوه; another cited poem has تق الله. The poets are unnamed in the source.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r3.anchor: وأنشدوا: 279 تقوه أيها الفتيان إني رأيت الله قد غلب الجدودا

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r4.claim: النار is the direct object of اتقوا and التي is its adjective; the source also cites poetic forms اللت and للت.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: { النار } مفعول به، و " التي " صفتها

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r5.claim: وقودها الناس is a nominal clause with a subject and predicate, serving as a relative clause with a resumptive pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r5.anchor: وقوله: { وقودها الناس } جملة من مبتدأ وخبر صلة وعائد

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r6.claim: The definite article in النار is anaphoric, recalling the Fire in Meccan al-Tahrim 66:6.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r6.anchor: والألف واللام في " النار " للعهد لتقدم ذكرها في سورة التحريم

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r7.claim: The prevalent fatḥa reading الوقود denotes fuel, the material used to kindle fire; another analysis treats it as a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r7.anchor: والمشهور فتح واو الوقود، وهو اسم ما يوقد به، وقيل: هو مصدر كالولوع

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r8.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r8.claim: Sibawayh is cited for limiting verbal nouns on the fuʿūl pattern to a short list including ولوع, قبول, وضوء and طهور; al-Kisa'i adds وزوع.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r8.anchor: ولم يجىء مصدر على فعول غير هذه الألفاظ فيما حكاه سيبويه. وزاد الكسائي

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r9.claim: A rare reading has ḍamma on وقود as a verbal noun; the source notes a parallel rare reading لغوب at Qaf 50:38 and Ibn Atiyya's report that both forms name fuel and a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r9.anchor: وقرئ شاذا في سورة (ق) { وما مسنا من لغوب } [الآية: 38]، فتصير سبعة

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r10.claim: If الوقود is a verbal noun rather than fuel, it needs an interpretation: intensive identification of the people with burning, or an omitted noun such as أصحاب or إحراق.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r10.anchor: أريد بهما المصدر فلا بد من تأويل وهو: إما المبالغة أي جعلوا نفس التوقد

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#2/r11.claim: The feminine pronoun ending in الحجارة marks the collective plural as feminine.

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r1.claim: أعدت is passive; its deputy subject is the pronoun referring to النار, so the feminine verb ending is required. A poetic counterexample is metrical necessity, against Ibn Kaysan.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r1.anchor: والقائم مقام الفاعل ضمير " النار " والتاء واجبة، لأن الفعل أسند إلى ضمير المؤنث

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r2.claim: للكافرين attaches to أعدت, which means prepared; a poem is cited as evidence for this meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r2.anchor: و " للكافرين " متعلق به، ومعنى أعدت: هيئت، قال: 284 أعددت للحدثان

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r3.claim: A variant reads أعتدت, from العتاد, with the sense of provision or preparation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r3.anchor: وقرئ: " أعتدت " من العتاد بمعنى العدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r4.claim: The clause is best treated as an independent answer to the implied question for whom the Fire was prepared; Abu al-Baqa instead makes it a circumstantial clause from النار, but the author objects that this is a permanent state.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r4.anchor: هذه الجملة الظاهر أنها لا محل لكونها مستأنفة جوابا لمن قال: لمن أعدت؟

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses أعدت للكافرين as a circumstantial clause from النار, governed by اتقوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " محلها النصب على الحال من " النار " ، والعامل فيها اتقوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects making it a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in وقودها: it is genitive after the noun, fuel is not an agent, and الناس intervenes between verbal noun and clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r6.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ولا يجوز أن تكون حالا من الضمير في " وقودها " لثلاثة أشياء

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r7.speaker: السجستاني
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r7.claim: Al-Sijistani makes أعدت للكافرين a second relative clause to التي, paralleling Al Imran 3:131.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r7.anchor: وقال السجستاني: { أعدت للكافرين } من صلة " التي " كقوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r8.claim: The author defends a possible second relative clause: وقودها الناس need not be a relative clause, since it could instead be parenthetical emphasis or a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:24#3/r8.anchor: قلت: ويمكن ألا يكون غلطا، لأنا لا نسلم أن { وقودها الناس } والحالة هذه صلة

ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r4.claim: The warning follows proof of divine unity and prophethood: they are threatened if they still refuse belief after the proof is established.
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r4.anchor: قيل لهم هذا بعد أن ثبت عليهم أمر التوحيد وأمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فوعدوا بالعذاب

ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r5.claim: Lam makes the future action carry a past sense, so the verb is jussive.
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r5.anchor: لم أحدثت في الفعل المستقبل معنى المضى فجزمته

ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r6.claim: Particles take inflectional effects proportionate to their meaning; lan and its clause are accusative because أن with its clause functions like a noun, unlike lam’s jussive clause.
ZAJJAJ:v1p100/r6.anchor: وكل حرف لزم الفعل فأحدث فيه معنى فله فيه من الإعراب

ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r1.claim: The fire is described through the most painful thing people know, conveying that divine punishment is among the severest kinds they know.
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r1.anchor: لا شيء في الدنيا أبلغ فيما يؤلم من النار، فقيل لهم إن عذاب الله من أشد الأجناس

ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r2.claim: The stones are said to be stones of sulfur.
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r2.anchor: ويقال إن الحجارة هنا تفسيرها حجارة الكبريت

ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r3.claim: Waqūd means firewood, or anything used to kindle a fire.
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r3.anchor: الوقود هو الحطب، وكل ما أوقد به فهو وقود

ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r4.claim: The verbal noun is normally pronounced with ḍamma, though fatḥa is also allowed; Arabic uses the pattern fuʿūl for a verbal noun.
ZAJJAJ:v1p101/r4.anchor: وقد روي وقدت النار وقودا وقبلت الشيء قبولا

ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r1.claim: The stones symbolize the lifelessness, powerlessness, and inefficacy of objects worshipped instead of God.
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r1.anchor: This evidently denotes all objects of worship to which men turn instead of God - their powerlessness and inefficacy being symbolized by the lifelessness of stones

ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r2.claim: “Human beings” stands for human actions that deviate from the way of truth.
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r2.anchor: the expression "human beings" stands here for human actions deviating from the way of truth

ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r3.claim: Remembering these objects and actions is bound to intensify the sinner’s suffering in the hereafter, called hell in the Qur’an.
ASAD-NOTES:2:23#n16/r3.anchor: the remembrance of all of which is bound to increase the sinner's suffering in the hereafter, referred to in the Qur'an as "hell"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p59/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p59/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p59/r1.claim: The section groups 2:24's challenge with 17:88's declaration that humans and jinn cannot produce the Qur'an's like, framing both as debate, challenge, and signs of inimitability.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p849/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p849/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p849/r3.claim: Omitting the objects of تفعلوا and لن تفعلوا leaves their scope formally unrestricted, although the immediate challenge makes the intended action clear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p849/r3.anchor: وهو أنه حذف مفعولين الفعلين المتعديين (تفعلوا) في قوله تعالى (فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا)

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r1.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف وعيسى الهمداني
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r1.claim: These readers have the variant وقودها الناس, whose vocalism prompts the author's syntactic explanation.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن بخلاف ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف1

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r2.claim: He parses the reading by ellipsis: ذو وقودها or أصحاب وقودها, since ḍamma-vocalized وقود is a verbal noun and people are not its action.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: هذا عندنا على حذف المضاف؛ أي: ذو وقودها، أو أصحاب وقودها الناس؛

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r3.claim: Although ḍamma is the normal verbal-noun form, Arabs exceptionally use fatḥa in وقود as in وقدت النار وقودا, alongside ولوعا and القبول.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r3.anchor: لكن قد جاء عنهم الوقود بالفتح في المصدر؛ لقولهم: وقدت النار وقودا،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r4.claim: Abu Bakr analyzes fatḥa-vocalized وضوء as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, not a verbal noun itself, because it means radiance.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r4.anchor: وكان أبو بكر يقول في قولهم: توضأت وضوءا: إن هذا المفتوح ليس مصدرا؛ وإنما هو صفة مصدر محذوف،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r5.claim: Abu ʿAlī applies Abu Bakr's analysis to ساكوت, while al-Aṣmaʿī's رجل بين الضارورة means between a co-wife or harm.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r5.anchor: وقرأت على أبي علي في نوادر أبي زيد: رجل ساكوت بين الساكوتة، فقال: قياس مذهب أبي بكر

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r6.claim: An unattested pattern may occur when attached to possessive ياء: al-Aʿshā's أيبلي is فَيْعلي, and تحوي from تحبة follows a similar pattern; this supports خصوصية and related forms.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p63/r6.anchor: فأيبلي كما ترى فيعلي، ولولا ياء الإضافة لم يجز ذلك،

NASHR:v2p27/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p27/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p27/r5.claim: Al-Dānī restricts retained ghunna before lām to cases where the nūn remains in the written form; he omits it when the muṣḥaf omits that nūn, as in the cited Hūd and al-Kahf examples.
NASHR:v2p27/r5.anchor: وهذا اختيار الحافظ أبي عمرو الداني، وغيره من المحققين، قال في جامع البيان: واختار في مذهب من يبقي الغنة مع الإدغام عند اللام

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p40#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p40#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p40#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies the fuel stones as sulfur stones, which God made however He willed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p40#2/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون عن ابن مسعود في قوله ﴿ وقودها الناس والحجارة ﴾ قال حجارة الكبريت جعلها الله كما شاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r5.claim: لن is a simple biconsonantal negator, not compounded from لا plus إن as al-Khalil reportedly held, nor does its ن replace an original alif as al-Farra held; it governs the subjunctive, though jussive use is reported.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r5.anchor: لن: حرف نفي ثنائي الوضع بسيط، لا مركب من لا إن خلافا للخليل في أحد قوليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r6.claim: لن does not entail perpetual negation, contrary to one Zamakhshari view; it is not shorter-lived than لا, limited to the near future, extended like لا, or a supplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r6.anchor: ولا يقتضي النفي على التأبيد خلافا للزمخشري في أحد قوليه، ولا هي أقصر نفيا من لا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r7.speaker: ابن الطراوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r7.claim: Some report jussive government by لن as a dialectal form; Ibn al-Tarawa cites a poem with يخب after لن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r7.anchor: وذكروا أن الجزم بها لغة، وأنشد ابن الطراوة: لن يخب الآن من رجائك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r8.claim: الوقود means fuel, what is used for kindling; it is also attested as a verbal noun, one of the rare nouns on the pattern فعول, alongside the forms listed by Ibn Asfur.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r8.anchor: الوقود: اسم لما يوقد به، وقد سمع مصدرا، وهو أحد المصادر التي جاءت على فعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r9.claim: الحجارة is the plural of حجر, and its feminine ending emphasizes the feminine plural, as in الفحولة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r9.anchor: الحجارة: جمع الحجر، والتاء فيها لتأكيد تأنيث الجمع كالفحولة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r10.claim: أعدت means prepared or made ready.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r13.claim: After arguing for God's oneness against shirk, the discourse addresses doubt about prophethood: the Quran is its proof as a miracle, tested by challenging eloquent Arabs and their allies to produce one surah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p165/r13.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه لما احتج تعالى عليهم بما يثبت الوحدانية ويبطل الإشراك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r6.claim: Because they cannot meet the challenge, the discourse turns from mockery to guidance, ordering them to avoid the fire prepared for those who deny.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r6.anchor: انتقل إلى إرشادهم، إذ ليسوا بقادرين على المعارضة، وأمرهم باتقاء النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r7.claim: إن rather than إذا continues the taunting challenge, like a speaker certain to win, or matches the opponents' own uncertainty before they reflect on the miracle and rely on eloquence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r7.anchor: وأتى بإن، وإن كان من مواضع إذا تهكما بهم، كما يقول القائل: إن غلبتك لم أبق عليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r8.claim: فإن لم تفعلوا means if you do not bring a surah; فعل is a general stand-in for any act and avoids spelling out the full phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r8.anchor: ومعنى: فإن لم تفعلوا فإن لم تأتوا، وعبر عن الإتيان بالفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r9.claim: Zamakhshari says فعل replaces الإتيان to avoid repeating the longer challenge wording; the author objects that إتيان could also be elided in both clauses, so the phrases are equivalent in ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: لو لم يعدل عن لفظ الإتيان إلى لفظ الفعل لاستطيل أن يقال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya oddly says لم is jussive because it resembles لا in negation: just as لا removes a noun's nunation, لم removes the verb's inflectional marker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p172/r10.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عطية تعليل غريب لعمل لم الجزم، قال: وجزمت لم لأنها أشبهت لا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r1.claim: The future challenge stirs their determination so their ensuing inability will be more striking; it proves prophethood both through the Quran's inimitability and the prediction that they will never match it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r1.anchor: وفي قوله: ولن تفعلوا إثارة لهممهم ليكون عجزهم بعد ذلك أبلغ وأبدع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r2.claim: Foreknowledge that the opponents would never meet the challenge belongs only to God; their failure to produce or report an answer despite hostile motives confirms the prediction as a miracle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r2.anchor: الإخبار بالغيب من أنهم لا لن يفعلوا، وهذا لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r3.claim: Musaylima and al-Mutanabbi did not attempt a literary counterchallenge; they claimed their crude, shallow, hybrid, badly composed texts were revelation, and God stripped them of eloquence for lying about Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r3.anchor: وأما ما أتى به مسيلمة الكذاب في هذره، وأبو الطيب المتنبي في عبره ونحوهما، فلم يقصدوا به المعارضة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r4.claim: ولن تفعلوا is an inserted clause with no syntactic position; it strengthens the prediction that the conditional failure will certainly occur, and its particle لن distinguishes it from a circumstantial clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r4.anchor: وقوله: ولن تفعلوا جملة اعتراض، فلا موضع لها من الإعراب، وفيها من تأكيد المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r5.claim: Zamakhshari says لن emphasizes future negation more strongly than لا, like a speaker's emphatic insistence; the author notes this conflicts with his other claim that لن negates forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r5.anchor: وما ذكره هنا مخالف لما حكي عنه أن لن تقتضي النفي على التأبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r6.speaker: ابن خطيب زملكاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r6.claim: Ibn Khatib Zamalakani says لن negates something near and does not extend indefinitely, nearly reversing Zamakhshari's account.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p173/r6.anchor: وأما ما ذهب إليه ابن خطيب زملكي من أن لن تنفي ما قرب وأن لا يمتد النفي فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says later scholars’ claims about emphasis, perpetuity, and denying the near future should yield to the authoritative Arab grammarians on particles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r1.anchor: وهذه الأقوال، أعني التوكيد والتأبيد ونفي ما قرب: أقاويل المتأخرين، وإنما المرجوع في معاني هذه الحروف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r2.claim: Sibawayh says lan negates the future of sa-yafʿalu, while lā negates the imperfect forms tafʿalu or lam tafʿal when intended as future.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r2.anchor: قال سيبويه، رحمه الله: ولن نفي لقوله: سيفعل، وقال: وتكون لا نفيا لقوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r3.claim: Although Sibawayh seems to restrict lā to future negation, its use in an exceptive, performative expression equivalent to illā can negate the present.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r3.anchor: وظاهر كلام سيبويه، رحمه الله، هنا أنها لا تنفي الحال، إلا أنه قد ذكر في الاستثناء من أدواته لا يكون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān favors al-Zamakhsharī’s first account: lan stresses denial by marking futurity overtly, while lā can also negate the present and is less specifically future.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r4.anchor: كان الأقرب من هذه الأقوال قول الزمخشري: أولا: من أن فيها توكيدا وتشديدا لأنها تنفي ما هو مستقبل بالأداة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r5.claim: The lan wording is more concise than wa-lā tafʿalūna, adding to its suitability for the challenge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p174/r5.anchor: ولأن ولن تفعلوا أخصر من ولا تفعلون، فلهذا كله ترجح النفي بلن على النفي بلا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r1.claim: The command to fear the Fire answers the conditional challenge and euphemistically means to stop obstinately resisting; those persisting after truth is clear deserve its punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r1.anchor: فاتقوا النار: جواب للشرط، وكنى به عن ترك العناد، لأن من عائد بعد وضوح الحق له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r2.claim: The Fire is definite because an indefinite fire was mentioned earlier in Meccan al-Taḥrīm, whereas this passage is Medinan; a repeated indefinite becomes definite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r2.anchor: وعرف النار هنا لأنه قد تقدم ذكرها نكرة في سورة التحريم، والتي في سورة التحريم نزلت بمكة، وهذه بالمدينة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r3.claim: The relative clause is familiar from the earlier description of a fire fueled by people and stones, or from what the People of the Book had heard before this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r3.anchor: والصلة معلومة للسامع لتقدم ذكر قوله: نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r4.claim: The majority read waqūduhā with an open wāw; al-Ḥasan is also reported to have a variant reading, which the passage does not specify.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r4.anchor: والجمهور على فتح الواو. وقرأ الحسن باختلاف، ومجاهد وطلحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r5.speaker: مجاهد وطلحة وأبو حياة وعيسى بن عمر الهمداني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r5.claim: These readers pronounce the wāw with ḍamma; this form is a verbal noun understood with an omitted muḍāf, or a forceful metaphor calling the people and stones the fuel itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r5.anchor: ومجاهد وطلحة وأبو حياة وعيسى بن عمر الهمداني بضم الواو.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r6.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmayr reads waqīdahā on the pattern faʿīl; like the majority reading, it means firewood or fuel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير وقيدها على وزن فعيل. فعلى قراءة الجمهور وقراءة ابن عمير هو الحطب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r7.claim: The description presents one distinctive Fire that actually burns people and stones, who are themselves what is consumed; it does not imply multiple fires.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r7.anchor: وهذه النار ممتازة عن غيرها بأنها تتقد بالناس والحجارة، وهما نفس ما يحرق، وظاهر هذا الوصف أنها نار واحدة ولا يدل على أنها نيران شتى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r8.claim: People means those God wills to enter the Fire despite the word’s general form; the stones are idols, paired with their worshippers as they were in earthly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r8.anchor: والناس يراد به الخصوص ممن شاء الله دخولها، وإن كان لفظه عاما، والحجارة الأصنام، وكانا وقودا للنار مقرونين معا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn Jurayj are cited for identifying the stones as sulfur, which ignites quickly, smells foul, produces much smoke, clings to bodies, and burns intensely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r9.anchor: روي ذلك عن ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وابن جريج. واختصت بذلك لما فيه من سرعة الالتهاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r10.claim: Other explanations identify the stones as black sulfur or special stones prepared for Hell whose fuel never runs out once kindled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو الكبريت الأسود، أو حجارة مخصوصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r1.claim: A report says a dark cloud will form when Hell’s inhabitants despair; they welcome it, but it rains huge millstone-like rocks that intensify the blaze.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r1.anchor: إن أهل النار إذا عيل صبرهم بكوا وشكوا، فينشىء الله سحابة سوداء مظلمة، فيرجون الفرج،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says the stones are the gold and silver people hoarded, which are cast into the Fire and used to brand them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r2.anchor: أو الحجارة ما اكتنزوه من الذهب والفضة تقذف معهم في النار ويكوون بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r3.claim: On the preceding interpretations, alif-lām in al-ḥijārah defines the kind rather than denoting every stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذه الأقوال لا تكون الألف واللام في الحجارة للعموم بل لتعريف الجنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r4.claim: Some scholars take the generic article comprehensively: the Fire is capable of burning anything of either kind, and the wording emphasizes Hell’s severity to intensify fear rather than describe actual fuel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r4.anchor: وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أنها تجوز أن تكون لاستغراق الجنس، ويكون المعنى أن النار التي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the capacity-only reading: the description states an actual event, and does not exclude jinn and devils also being in the Fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r5.anchor: وما ذهب إليه هذا الذاهب من أن هذا الوصف هو بالصلاحية لا بالفعل غير ظاهر، بل الظاهر أن هذا الوصف واقع لا محالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r6.claim: People precede stones because they are rational and feel pain, may be more combustible through their bodily materials, or make a more frightening spectacle when burned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r6.anchor: وقدم الناس على الحجارة لأنهم العقلاء الذين يدركون الآلام والمعذبون، أو لكونهم أكثر إيقادا للنار من الجماد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the word “prepared” refutes the claim that the Fire has not yet been created; he attributes that view to Mundhir ibn Saʿīd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p175#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وفي قوله تعالى: أعدت رد على من قال: إن النار لم تخلق حتى الآن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r1.speaker: أهل السنة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r1.claim: Ahl al-Sunna hold that Paradise and Hell have truly been created already.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r1.anchor: أن مذهب أهل السنة أن الجنة والنار مخلوقتان على الحقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r2.speaker: كثير من المعتزلة والجهمية والنجاومية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r2.claim: Many Muʿtazilites, Jahmites, and Nujāmiyya say Paradise and Hell have not yet been created and will be created later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r2.anchor: وذهب كثير من المعتزلة والجهمية والنجاومية إلى أنهما لم يخلقا بعد، وأنهما سيخلقان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r3.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads iʿtaddat, from ʿatād, meaning equipment or provision.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله اعتدت: من العتاد بمعنى العدة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r4.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r4.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads “God prepared it for the unbelievers.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: أعدها الله للكافرين، ولا يدل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r5.claim: Mentioning unbelievers does not mean that only they enter this Fire or that sinners face a different Fire; the addressees are included, unbelievers are the majority, and believers are not destined to remain there forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r5.anchor: ولا يدل إعدادها للكافرين على أنهم مخصوصون بها، كما ذهب إليه بعض المتأولين من أن نار العصاة غير نار الكفار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r6.claim: A sound hadith establishes that a group of major sinners will enter the Fire; the author says unbelievers may be named because they predominate in the address or the term covers denial of God and His blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r6.anchor: وقد ثبت في الحديث الصحيح إدخال طائفة من أهل الكبائر النار، لكنه اكتفى بذكر الكفار تغليبا للأكثر على الأقل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses “prepared for the unbelievers” as a circumstantial clause governed by “fear the Fire.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r7.anchor: والجملة من قوله: أعدت للكافرين في موضع الحال من النار، والعامل فيها: فاتقوا، قاله أبو البقاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that this makes the circumstantial state permanent and pointless: the Fire is prepared whether people fear it or not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك نظر، لأن جعله الجملة حالا يصير المعنى: فاتقوا النار في حال إعدادها للكافرين، وهي معدة للكافرين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r9.claim: He prefers an ungoverned sentence answering an implied question: after hearing the Fire’s fuel described, the listener asks for whom it was prepared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p176/r9.anchor: والأولى عندي أن تكون الجملة لا موضع لها من الإعراب، وكأنها سؤال جواب مقدر كأنه لما وصفت بأن وقودها الناس والحجارة قيل: لمن أعدت؟

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r1.claim: After maximal effort still fails to produce anything comparable, the challenge establishes the Qur’an’s miraculousness and makes belief and Godfearing obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r1.anchor: إذا بذلتم في السعي غاية المجهود وجاوزتم في الحد كل حد معهود متشبثين بالذيول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r2.claim: The conditional particle despite their certain inability taunts them and exposes their foolish reliance on eloquence; it may be ironic metaphor, literal, or a convention contrary to the apparent situation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r2.anchor: وأتى بأن والمقام اذا العجز وهو سبحانه وتعالى اللطيف الخبير تهكما بهم كما يقول الواثق بالغلبة لخصمه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham denies syntactic competition between particles because they do not denote events and therefore do not seek complements.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r3.anchor: وقد صرح إبن هشام بأنه لا يكون بين الحروف لأنها لا دلالة لها على الحدث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r4.speaker: إبن العلج
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r4.claim: Ibn al-ʿAlj allows competition between إن and لم on the basis of this verse, but the author reports the objection that they differ in polarity, violating the condition of semantic sameness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r4.anchor: إلا أن إبن العلج أجازه إستدلالا بهذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r5.claim: The author explains their coexistence by taking إن to govern the whole clause, as though it said, “if you abandon the act”; this yields continued failure beginning in the past.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r5.anchor: فإن هنا داخلة على المجموع عاملة في محله كأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r6.claim: He leaves an unresolved parsing problem: it is unclear whether the syntactic locus belongs to the verb, the clause, or both, and extracting a verb from what follows seems unsatisfactory.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r6.anchor: قيل في ذلك إشكال لم يحرر دفعه بعد بما يشفي العليل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r7.claim: The generic “act” concisely makes attempting the commanded feat the test, since producing the object is impossible; the conditional consequence follows their inability to perform it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r7.anchor: عبر سبحانه عن الفعل الخاص حيث كان الظاهر فإن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله بالفعل المطلق العام ظاهرا لإيجاز القصر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r8.claim: An alternative takes “act” as naming the necessary act while intending its associated object, or as avoiding repetition by replacing an explicit noun with a pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p197/r8.anchor: أطلق الفعل وأريد به الإتيان مع ما يتعلق به على طريقة ذكر اللازم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r1.claim: لن denies a future event, specializes in the imperfect, and governs the subjunctive, though a poetic exception is cited; it does not by itself make the denial eternal.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r1.anchor: ( لن ) يخب الآن من رجاك ومن حرك من دون بابك الحلقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r2.claim: Although لن adds emphasis and force, the author rejects claims that it entails perpetual negation or a long or short duration.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r2.anchor: ولا تقتضي النفي على التأييد وإن أفادت التأكيد والتشديد ولا طول مدة أو قلتها خلافا لبعضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r3.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r3.claim: A derivation reported from al-Khalil makes لن originate in أن: the hamza was dropped through frequent use, then the alif at the meeting of two quiescent letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r3.anchor: روى عن الخليل : فحذفت الهمزة لكثرتها وسقطت الألف للساكنين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r4.claim: A poetic line containing لا أن is offered for the derivation, but the possibility that أن is extra weakens its evidentiary force.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r4.anchor: يرجى المرء ما ( لا أن ) يلاقيه ويعرض دون أقربه الخطوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r5.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives لن from لا with its alif changed to nūn; the author rejects this as unmotivated and contrary to the ordinary principle.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r5.anchor: ولا لاكما عند الفراء فأبدلت ألفه نونا إذ لا داعي إلى ذلك وهو خلاف الأصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r6.claim: The promise of future inability is parenthetical between the two parts of the conditional, reinforcing its premise and the obligation in its consequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r6.anchor: والجملة إعتراض بين جزئي الشرطية ظاهرا مقرر لمضمون مقدمها ومؤكد لإيجاب العمل بتاليها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r7.claim: The categorical prediction is a manifest miracle of foreknowledge: a comparable challenge would have been widely transmitted given the motive to report it; Musaylima’s words were not meant as a contest.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r7.anchor: وهذه معجزة باهرة حيث أخبر بالغيب الخاص علمه به سبحانه وقد وقع الأمر كذلك كيف لا ولو عارضوه بشيء يدانيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r8.claim: The imperative is the conditional answer; avoiding the Fire can stand for recognizing the miracle and believing in it, or for faith itself, so its conditional attachment is meaningful.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r8.anchor: جواب للشرط على أن إلتقاء النار كناية عن ظهور إعجازه المقتضي للتصديق والإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r9.claim: This interpretation answers the objection that avoidance of Hell is always required and that inability to produce a match is neither its cause nor necessary condition; some instead posit an implicit answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r9.anchor: يندفع ما يتوهم من أن إتقاء النار لازم من غير توقف على هذا الشرط فما معنى التعليق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r10.claim: With fatḥa, وقود ordinarily means fuel, the thing by which a fire is lit; the form فعول commonly names an instrument or thing acted upon, though it can be a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r10.anchor: والوقود بالفتح كما قرأ به الجمهور ما يوقد به النار وكذا كل ما كان على فعول أسم لما يفعل به في المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r11.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r11.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads وقيدها, a variant the author records without further argument.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r12.speaker: عيسى بن عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r12.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAmr and others read the word with ḍamma; if it is a noun for fuel, its sense matches the common reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r12.anchor: وعيسى بن عمرو وغيره ( وقودها ) بالضم فإن كان اسما لما يوقد به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r13.claim: If the ḍamma reading is a verbal noun, its predication of the Fire is explained by emphasis, figurative transfer or comparison, or an implied possessive or burning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198/r13.anchor: وإن كان مصدراكما قيل في سائر ما كان على فعول فحمله على النار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.claim: Alusi reports Ibn Mālik’s analysis: حجارة is the plural of حجر, with أحجار as the paucity plural; Ibn Mālik calls حجارة a collective noun because its pattern commonly occurs among singular nouns, which Alusi finds apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r1.anchor: إنه اسم جمع لغلبة وزنه في المفردات وهو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd identify the stones as sulfur; the author says this is the sounder view among hadith scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بها على ما صح عن إبن عباس وإبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنهم ولمثل ذلك حكم الرفع حجارة الكبريت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.claim: Sulfur intensifies the Fire through extreme heat, rapid ignition, adhesion to bodies, and the inmates’ becoming fuel; its stench, smoke, and density heighten the warning, though the next world exceeds worldly comparison.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r3.anchor: وفيها من شدة الحر وكثرة الإلتهاب وسرعة الإيقاد ومزيد الإلتصاق بالأبدان وإعداد أهل النار أن يكونوا حطبا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies the stones as carved idols, joined with their worshippers to increase their remorse when events contradict their expectations.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r4.anchor: المراد بها الأصنام التي ينحتونها وقرنها بهم في الآخرة زيادة لتحسرهم حيث بدا لهم نقيض ما كانوا يتوقعون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r5.claim: The idol interpretation is supported by the verse saying that worshippers and what they worship apart from God are Hell’s fuel; Ibn ʿArabī’s words also hint at it.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r6.claim: A lexicon-based proposal takes the stones to mean gold and silver, which are also called حجر; the author regards it as weaker than the sulfur and idol readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r6.anchor: وحملها على الذهب والفضة لأنهما يسميان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r7.claim: Among the two stronger identifications, hadith scholars prefer sulfur, whereas Zamakhsharī prefers the idol interpretation and Ibn ʿArabī hints at it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r7.anchor: الأصح أولهما عند المحدثين وثانيهما عند الزمخشري

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r8.claim: The definite article on Fire is not, in the author’s view, generic; some scholars take it universally, meaning the Fire is fully capable of consuming both kinds of fuel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r8.anchor: وأل فيها على كل ليست للعموم وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أنها له ويكون المعنى أن النار التي وعدوا بها صالحة لأن تحرق ما ألقى فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r9.claim: Naming people and stones magnifies Hell’s severity and makes the warning more frightening; a nonliteral reading conflicts with the apparent verses and risks impugning divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r9.anchor: تعظيما لشأن جهنم وتنبيها على شدة وقودها ليقع ذلك من النفوس أعظم موقع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r10.claim: Mentioning only people and stones does not exclude jinn and devils from Hell, since other passages establish their presence there.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r10.anchor: ولا يتوهم من الإقتصار على هذين الجنسين أن لا يكون في النار غيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r11.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿArabī says people are Hell’s flames and idols its embers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r11.anchor: قال سيدي الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره : أنهم لهبها وأولئك جمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r12.claim: People precede stones because they perceive pain, or because their flesh, fat, and skin make them more combustible, intensifying the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r12.anchor: وبدأ سبحانه بالناس لأنهم الذين يدركون الآلام أو لكونهم أكثر إيقادا من الجماد لما فيهم من الجلود واللحوم والشحوم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r13.claim: Fire is definite as an already known story because the description had appeared in Sūrat al-Taḥrīm; the author notes that the claim that al-Taḥrīm came first is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r13.anchor: لأن المنكر في سورة التحريم نزل أولا فسمعوه بصفته فلما نزل هذا بعد جاء معهودا فعرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r14.claim: The preparation clause is detached from the preceding relative description to give the warning independent emphasis, as an independent statement of the Fire’s preparation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r14.anchor: إبتداء كلام قطع عما قبله مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن يعطف على الصلة السابقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r15.claim: Making the clause an answer to “why is its fuel so?” fails because the context does not prompt that question and the answer does not explain it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r15.anchor: أما الثاني فلأن المقصد من الصلة التهويل فالسؤال بلم كان شأن النار كذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r16.claim: Parsing أعدت as a circumstantial clause from Fire, with an implied قد, is weak: its restriction is unnatural, and taking its predicate from the preceding clause creates an awkward separation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p198#2/r16.anchor: وجعله حالا من النار بإضمار قد والخبر من أجزاء الصلة لذي الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r1.speaker: الإمام المرزوقي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r1.claim: Al-Marzūqī allows أعدت as a second relative clause; multiple clauses of description or predication may occur with or without a conjunction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r1.anchor: إنها صلة بعد صلة وتعدد الصلات كالصفات والأخبار كثير بعاطف وبدونه كما نص عليه الإمام المرزوقي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: Ibn Mālik allows coordination with the conjunction omitted; treating وقودها الناس as parenthetical or circumstantial is an unsuitable parsing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: أو معطوف بحذف الحرف كما صرح به إبن مالك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: ومعنى ( أعدت ) هيئت وقرأ عبد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads أعتدت, from العتاد, meaning preparation or provision.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله أعتدت من العتاد بمعنى العدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r5.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads أعدها الله, explicitly naming God as the one who prepared it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r5.anchor: وإبن أبي عبلة أعدها الله للكافرين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r6.claim: The phrase may mean disbelievers as a class, with the addressees included foremost, or these addressees alone; an explicit noun can replace their pronoun to censure and explain the judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r6.anchor: والمراد إما جنسهم والمخاطبون داخلون فيهم دخولا أوليا أو هم خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r7.claim: Preparation for disbelievers does not bar others from entering incidentally, so there is no need to posit a different Fire for sinful believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r7.anchor: وكون الأعداد للكافرين لا ينافي دخول غيرهم فيها على جهة التطفل فلا حاجة إلى القول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r8.claim: The apparent verse indicates that Hell is already created; treating the future as a completed past because it is certain, as the Muʿtazilites do, is against the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r8.anchor: يتبادر من الآية الكريمة أن النار مخلوقة الآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r9.speaker: أهل الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r9.claim: People of spiritual unveiling hold that Hell is created but unfinished: it is presently burning air without embers, its keepers praise God, and human and jinn deeds produce its pains and changing punishments.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r9.anchor: والذي ذهب أهل الكشف إليه أنها مخلوقة غير أنها لم تتم وهي الآن عندهم دار حرروها هواء محترق لا جمر لها البتة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r10.speaker: عبدالله بن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r10.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, seeing the sea, asked when it would become fire, disliked ablution with its water, and preferred dry ablution, citing the oceans being kindled.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r10.anchor: عبدالله بن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r11.claim: The author describes bodily fire affecting the body’s exterior senses and a spiritual fire reaching hearts and punishing the directing soul; arrogant ignorance of God is itself severe torment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r11.anchor: وهي ناران حسية مسلطة على ظاهر الجسم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r12.claim: The exact state of the afterlife cannot be known by people immersed in worldly ties; accept what the truthful Prophet reported when it is not impossible and entrust its reality to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p199/r12.anchor: وحقيقة الأمر عندي لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى ولا شيء أحسن من التسليم لما جاء به النبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r4.claim: The challenge means they had failed already and would never succeed in the future, demonstrating the Quran's inimitability and its status as the Prophet's miracle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r4.anchor: أبدا فيما بقي. وإنما قال ذلك لبيان الإعجاز وأن القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r5.claim: Taking refuge from the Fire means believing in order to be protected from it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and most exegetes identify the fuel stones as sulfur, since sulfur catches fire more readily.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين يعني حجارة الكبريت لأنها أكثر التهابا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r7.claim: One view takes the stones to mean stones in general, underscoring the Fire's immense size.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: جميع الحجارة وهو دليل على عظمة تلك النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r8.claim: Another view identifies the stones as idols, since most of the worshippers' idols were carved from stone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: أراد بها الأصنام لأن أكثر أصنامهم كانت منحوتة من الحجارة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r9.claim: The Fire has been prepared for the disbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p72#3/r9.anchor: كما قال "إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم" (98-الأنبياء) {أعدت} هيئت {للكافرين}

BURSEVI:v1p61/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p61/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p61/r7.claim: The challenge predicts that they will never produce a like sura, since the Quran's inimitability is manifest.
BURSEVI:v1p61/r7.anchor: وذلك لظهور إعجاز القرآن فإنه معجزة النبي عليه السلام اعتراض بين الشرط

BURSEVI:v1p61/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p61/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p61/r8.claim: Their inability establishes that Muhammad is God's messenger and the Quran His book; rejecting belief leaves them liable to Hell.
BURSEVI:v1p61/r8.anchor: ولما عجزتم عن معارضة القرآن ومثله لزمتكم الحجة أن محمدا رسولي والقرآن كتابي

BURSEVI:v1p62/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r1.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v1p62/r1.claim: Al-Kashshāf says fearing the Fire entails abandoning obstinacy, so the command to fear it stands for giving up stubborn opposition.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r1.anchor: وفي "الكشاف" : لصيق اتقاء النار وضميمه ترك العناد

BURSEVI:v1p62/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r2.claim: The Fire's waqūd is its fuel, the material with which it is kindled.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r2.anchor: {التى وقودها} أي : حطبها وهو ما يوقد به النار

BURSEVI:v1p62/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r3.claim: The people serving as fuel are the sinful.

BURSEVI:v1p62/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r4.claim: The stones may be sulfur stones, which kindle quickly, burn out slowly, and cause intense heat, foul smell, and bodily adhesion.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r4.anchor: وإنما جعل حطبها منها لسرعة وقودها أي : التهابها وبطء خمودها وشدة حرها

BURSEVI:v1p62/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r5.claim: Alternatively, the stones are the idols worshipped by the disbelievers, who are punished through the objects they trusted and revered.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r5.anchor: أو الحجارة هي الأصنام التي عبدوها وإنما جعل التعذيب بها ليتحققوا

BURSEVI:v1p62/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r6.claim: Being punished alongside the idols and leaders they served makes the followers' punishment harder and extinguishes their hopes in them.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r6.anchor: كأتباع الكبراء خدموهم ورجوهم وفي النار يسحبون معهم

BURSEVI:v1p62/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r7.claim: The whole Fire is not fueled this way; there are different fires, including one fueled by people and stones.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r7.anchor: قلت : بل هي نار شتى منها نار توقد بالناس والحجارة

BURSEVI:v1p62/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62/r8.claim: By analogy, the fire for unbelieving jinn and their devils may be fueled by demons, matching each group with its kind of punishment.
BURSEVI:v1p62/r8.anchor: ولعل لكفار الجن ولشياطينهم نارا وقودها الشياطين كما أن لكفرة الإنس نارا

BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r1.claim: The Fire has been prepared as punishment for those who disbelieve what God revealed.
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r1.anchor: هيئت للذين كفروا بما نزلناه وجعلت عدة لعذابهم

BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r2.claim: The verse indicates that the Fire is created and already exists, against the Muʿtazilites.
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r2.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن النار مخلوقة موجودة الآن خلافا للمعتزلة

BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r3.claim: Accepting the Quran and Muhammad brings deliverance from the Fire and further demonstrates the merit of the Quran and its people.
BURSEVI:v1p62#2/r3.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن ثمرة الأخذ بالقرآن والإقرار به وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم هو النجاة من النار

BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r1.claim: In the inward reading, the Fire signifies divine overpowering and the form of God's wrath, as God calls it His punishment.
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r1.anchor: هي القهر وصورة غضب الحق كما قال

BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r2.claim: The people fueling it signify human selfhood, whose defining trait is forgetting God.
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r2.anchor: أنانية الإنسان التي نسيان الله من خصوصيتها

BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r3.claim: The stones signify gold, which fulfills the ego's desires and what its appetites crave.
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r3.anchor: أي : الذهب لأنه به يحصل مرادات النفس وشهواتها وما يميل إليه الهوى

BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r4.claim: Selfhood and gold become fuel because people seek and worship what is other than God, forgetting the Truth and the primordial covenant.
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r4.anchor: لأنها إنما طلبت غير الله وعبدته لنسيان الحق ومعاهدة يوم الميثاق

BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r5.claim: The Fire is prepared especially for unbelievers, but sinful believers may enter it by following them; believers later enter Paradise after purification.
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r5.anchor: ولكن يظهر المذنبون بها بتبعية الكافرين كما أن الجنة خلقت وأعدت للمتقين

BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r6.claim: The Prophet quotes God as saying that Paradise and Hell were created for their respective people, who act in the manner of each.
BURSEVI:v1p62#3/r6.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حكاية عن الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r1.claim: If they cannot match the Qur’an after striving, its inimitability is proven and belief obligatory; they should fear the punishment prepared for deniers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r1.anchor: ظهر أنه معجز والتصديق به واجب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r2.claim: The broad verb ‘do’ concisely stands for producing a comparable revelation, an act that encompasses the specific challenge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r2.anchor: فعبر عن الإتيان المكيف بالفعل الذي يعم الإتيان وغيره إيجازا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r3.claim: Stating the necessary consequence in place of the implied result alludes to the proof, magnifies obstinacy, and makes the threat explicit with brevity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r3.anchor: ونزل لازم الجزاء منزلته على سبيل الكناية تقريرا للمكنى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r4.claim: The conditional uses إن, though the situation calls for اذا, because God does not doubt their inability; the denial interrupts condition and consequence in mockery, addressing their pre-consideration belief that they might succeed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r4.anchor: فإن القائل سبحانه وتعالى لم يكن شاكا في عجزهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r5.claim: لم governs the jussive because it is restricted to the imperfect and attached to its complement; since it makes the verb past-like, the conditional applies to the combined phrase as ‘if you leave the act.’

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r6.claim: لن negates the future more emphatically than لا.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r6.anchor: كلا في نفي المستقبل غير أنه أبلغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r7.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r7.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalil, in one reported account, treat لن as a primitive particle; in another account from al-Khalil, it derives from لا أن.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r7.anchor: وهو حرف مقتضب عند سيبويه والخليل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r8.speaker: الفراء
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ analyzes لن as لا with its alif replaced by نون.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r8.anchor: وعند الفراء لا فأبدلت ألفها نونا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r9.claim: With fatḥa, وقود means the fuel by which a fire is kindled; with ḍamma it is the verbal noun, though the verbal noun can also take fatḥa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r9.anchor: والوقود بالفتح ما توقد به النار

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r10.speaker: سيبويه
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r10.claim: Sibawayh reports the expression وقدت النار وقودا عاليا; the ḍamma form is a noun, perhaps a verbal noun used as a noun, and is also read here.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r10.anchor: قال سيبويه: وسمعنا من يقول وقدت النار وقودا عاليا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r11.claim: The apparent sense is the noun ‘fuel’; if it is instead a verbal noun, an omitted مضاف is understood: ‘its fuel is the burning of people.’

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r12.claim: حجارة is a plural of حجر, like جمالة from جمل, an uncommon, nonproductive plural pattern.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r12.anchor: وهي جمع حجر. كجمالة جمع جمل وهو قليل غير منقاس

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r13.claim: The stones are the idols the people carved and worshiped alongside themselves, hoping for their intercession, benefit, and protection from harm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24/r13.anchor: والمراد بها الأصنام التي نحتوها وقرنوا بها أنفسهم وعبدوها طمعا في شفاعتها والانتفاع بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.claim: He supports identifying the stones as idols with the verse saying that the people and what they worship besides God are hell’s fuel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.anchor: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that they are punished by the source of their crime, just as hoarders are punished by what they hoarded; another is that punishment reverses their expectations and heightens regret.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.anchor: أو بنقيض ما كانوا يتوقعون زيادة في تحسرهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.claim: An alternative identifies the stones as the gold and silver people hoarded and trusted in; al-Bayḍāwī objects that this would not explain why this punishment is specified for disbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: الذهب والفضة التي كانوا يكنزونها ويغترون بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says the stones are sulfur; al-Bayḍāwī rejects this as an unsupported restriction that undercuts the verse’s aim of magnifying the fire, while suggesting Ibn ʿAbbās may mean all its stones act like sulfur in ordinary fires.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.anchor: فإن صح هذا عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما فلعله عني به

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.claim: Because this Medinan verse followed the Meccan statement that people and stones fuel the Fire, its definite reference is understood as familiar to its audience; the linked sentence presupposes a known story.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.anchor: ولما كانت الآية مدنية نزلت بعد ما نزل بمكة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.claim: The Fire has been prepared and set aside as their punishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r2.claim: A variant reads أعتدت, from العتاد, meaning equipment or provision.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.claim: The clause may be a resumption or a circumstantial clause of النار with an implicit قد; it cannot refer to the pronoun in وقودها if وقود is a verbal noun, because a predicate separates them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.anchor: والجملة استئناف، أو حال بإضمار قد من النار

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.claim: The challenge and threat urge strenuous counteraction, yet even against the shortest surah, a numerous, eloquent, fiercely hostile audience did not reply with a countertext and instead left home and risked their lives; this proves prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.anchor: ما فيهما من التحدي والتحريض على الجد وبذل الوسع في المعارضة بالتقريع والتهديد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.claim: The verse foretells the unseen: any successful countertext would normally have remained known, especially since critics outnumbered defenders in every age.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.anchor: يتضمنان الإخبار عن الغيب على ما هو به

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.claim: Were the Prophet uncertain, he would not have challenged them so emphatically, lest a counterargument overturn his proof.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.anchor: لو شك في أمره لما دعاهم إلى المعارضة بهذه المبالغة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.claim: The wording indicates that the Fire already exists, prepared now for the disbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.anchor: دل على أن النار مخلوقة معدة الآن لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r19.claim: The conditional 'if you do not' grants them a respite in wording and mocks their presumed ability, exposing their ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r19.anchor: فأتى بأداة الشك تنفيسا لهم وتهكما في نفس الأمر بهم واستجهالا لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r20.claim: The emphatic prediction then strikes decisively: God rules that they will fail, and their silence confirms the verdict across every age.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r20.anchor: ثم لم يتمم ذلك التنفيس حتى ضربهم ضربة فضمت ظهورهم وقطعت قلوبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r21.claim: They had no effective response except to stop attempting the challenge, thereby verifying the prophecy of failure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r21.anchor: فلم يكن لهم فعل إلا المبادرة إلى تصديقه بالكف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r22.claim: The word 'do' is broader than 'bring': denying the general act also denies the more specific act of producing a rival.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r22.anchor: والتعبير بالفعل الأعم من الإتيان أبلغ لأن نفيه نفي الأخص وزيادة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r23.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r23.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines action as what appears from a prompting circumstance, whether done knowingly or not, religiously or otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p63/r23.anchor: والفعل قال الحرالي ما ظهر عن داعية من الموقع كان عن علم أو غير علم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes the Fire as a subtle substance whose extreme action reverses ordinary states through intense heat or cold.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي , وهي جوهر لطيف يفرط لشدة لطافته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r5.claim: Another definition calls it a luminous, hot body whose nature is to burn.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r5.anchor: جسم لطيف مضيء حار من شأنه الإحراق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r6.claim: The stones include the idols the opponents paired with themselves in worldly worship; their failure and continued denial make them obstinate, and their idols will burn them without benefit or intercession.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r6.anchor: التي هي أعم من أصنامهم التي قرنوا بها أنفسهم في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r7.claim: The definite 'Fire' and its relative description present the Qur'an's divinely established report as certain, as though even what the audience does not know is universally known.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r7.anchor: وتعريف النار وصلة الموصول لأن أخبار القرآن بعد ثبوت أنه من عند الله معلومة مقطوع بها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains stone as what has become hard through the compact joining of its water and earth components.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r8.anchor: الحجارة ما تحجر أي اشتد تصام أجزائه من الماء والتراب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r9.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses 'fear' as stopping the separation of God from His Messenger: they acknowledge God's lordship while doubting His Messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r9.anchor: واتقوا } أي توقفوا عن هذه التفرقة بين الله ورسوله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees the punishment as a fitting, painful separation of what should be joined; if they missed restraint guided by knowledge, they should heed restraint driven by pain.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r10.anchor: فإنها نار غذاؤها واشتعالها بالكون كله أنهاه تركيبا وهم الناس الملائمون لمارجها بالنوس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r11.claim: Its human and stone fuel spans the extremes of created beings and implies a scope and power beyond worldly fire, which is fueled by plants and affects extremes only indirectly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p69/r11.anchor: وليست كنار الدنيا التي غذاؤها من ضعيف الموالد وهو النبات ولا تفعل في الطرفين إلا بواسطة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r1.claim: Al-Ḥarālī cites the fire brought from the green tree in Yā Sīn 36:80 and the Arab saying that every tree contains fire, especially marakh and ʿafār.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r1.anchor: وتقول العرب : في كل شجر نار واستمجد المرخ والعفار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r2.claim: The word 'fuel' points to what fire acts on most intensely, since it mediates the fire's action on everything else; consuming the fuel strengthens the fire against it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r2.anchor: لأن النار أشد فعلها في وقودها لأن بتوسطه تفعل فيما سواه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the punished are conceived as both generated from and nourished by the Fire; it is hidden in them in worldly life and blazing in the afterlife, each person bearing its measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r3.anchor: ويفهم اعتبارها بنار الدنيا انقداحها من أعمال المجزيين بها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r4.claim: Al-Biqāʿī supports the fiery-element analogy with the description of wasteful people as satanic brothers and the devils' incitement of unbelievers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r4.anchor: أي في أن الغالب عليهم العنصر الناري

BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes the stones to imply resurrection and judgment for all that the heavens and earth contain, not only humans and jinn; all creation is divided between Garden and Fire as between good and vile.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r5.anchor: وفي ذكر الحجارة إفهام عموم البعث والجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says belief initially emphasizes resurrection and recompense of the two weighty kinds for ease; belief about the rest is an increase and completion of faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p70/r6.anchor: وإنما اقتصر في مبدأ عقيدة الإيمان على الإيمان ببعث الثقلين وجزائهم تيسيرا واستفتاحا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r1.speaker: بعض العلماء
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r1.claim: Some scholars restrict resurrection and recompense to humans and jinn, deny reward to other creatures, and strain to reinterpret the report that a hornless sheep will receive justice from a horned sheep.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r1.anchor: حتى أن منهم من ينكر جزاء ما سواهما

BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r2.claim: The Prophet reports that the hornless sheep will receive redress from the horned sheep.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r2.anchor: يقتص للشاة الجماء من الشاة القرناء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r3.claim: The Fire has been prepared and made ready before it is used, and it is prepared for the disbelievers and anyone who shares their trait of concealing God's signs.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r4.claim: The passive voice leaves the preparer unnamed; al-Biqāʿī says an unknown perpetrator makes the complainant's grievance more painful.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r4.anchor: وتقاد للمجهول لأن المشتكي إذا جهل فاعله كان أنكأ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī compares this prepared punishment to a worldly king's sword kept ready for its intended victims.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p71/r5.anchor: وهي عدة الملك الديان لهم بمنزلة سيف الملك من ملوك الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the failure to meet the challenge has made the truth clear to them.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وادعوا شهداءكم} قال: أعوانكم على ما أنتم عليه {فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا} فقد بين لكم الحق

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r3.claim: Qatada explains that they will neither be able nor have strength to meet the challenge.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا} يقول: لن تقدروا على ذلك ولن تطيقوه

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r4.claim: Ibn Masud recommends seeking refuge from hell when its mention occurs in prayer and asking God for Paradise when it is mentioned.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إذا مر أحدكم في الصلاة بذكر النار فلسيتعذ بالله من النار وإذا مر أحدكم بذكر الجنة فليسأل الله الجنة

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r5.speaker: أبو ليلى
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r5.claim: Abu Layla reports that the Prophet sought refuge from the Fire and warned woe to its inhabitants when he passed a verse during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r5.anchor: عن أبي ليلى قال صليت إلى جنب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فمر بآية فقال: أعوذ بالله من النار ويل لأهل النار

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r6.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r6.claim: Al-Numan ibn Bashir heard the Prophet repeatedly warn from the pulpit about the Fire, so forcefully that a cloak edge fell from his shoulders.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r6.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو على المنبر يقول: أنذركم النار أنذركم النار حتى سقط أحد عطفي ردائه على منكبيه

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r7.claim: Mujahid read the Qur'anic form with the first wāw in the nominative except in 85:5, where he read it in the accusative.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه كان يقرأ كل شيء في القرآن {وقودها} برفع الواو الأولى إلا التي في والسماء ذات البروج (النار ذات الوقود)

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r8.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the stones as sulfur created by God as He willed; al-Hakim authenticated this report.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن الحجارة التي ذكرها الله في القرآن في قوله {وقودها الناس والحجارة} حجارة من كبريت

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says they are black sulfur stones in the Fire with which people are punished alongside its flames.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: هي حجارة في النار من كبريت أسود يعذبون به مع النار

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r10.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
