DURR-FULL:v1p89/r10.claim: Amr ibn Maymun says the sulfur stones were created with the heavens and earth in the lowest heaven and prepared for disbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r10.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون قال: هي حجارة من كبريت خلقها الله يوم خلق السموات والأرض في السماء الدنيا فأعدها للكافرين

DURR-FULL:v1p89/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r11.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r11.claim: Anas attributes to the Prophet the report that Hell was kindled for three thousand years, turning red, then white, then black, and remains dark and unquenchable.
DURR-FULL:v1p89/r11.anchor: عن أنس قال تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية {وقودها الناس والحجارة} فقال: أوقد عليها ألف عام حتى احمرت

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports from the Prophet that Hell was kindled for a thousand years each until red, white, then black, leaving it black and dark.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أوقدت النار ألف سنة حتى احمرت ثم أوقد عليها ألف سنة حتى ابيضت

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's comparison that human fire is one seventieth of Hellfire; its other sixty-nine portions each have the same heat.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال نار بني آدم التي توقدون جزء من سبعين جزء من نار جهنم

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Fire is blacker than pitch, rather than red like familiar fire.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أترونها حمراء مثل ناركم هذه التي توقدون إنها لأشد سوادا من القار

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r4.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet's statement that worldly fire is one of seventy parts of Hellfire, each part bearing its heat.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم لكل جزء منها حرها

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying worldly fire is one seventieth of Hellfire, was cooled with water twice, and asks God not to return it to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r5.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم لولا أنها أطفئت بالماء مرتين

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r6.claim: Ibn Masud says worldly fire is one seventieth of Hellfire and would be unusable had it not been plunged in the sea twice.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من تلك النار ولولا أنها ضربت في البحر مرتين

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports from the Prophet that worldly fire was struck with sea water twice, which made it useful to people.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم ضربت بماء البحر مرتين

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r8.claim: Mujahid says this worldly fire seeks refuge from Hellfire.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: إن ناركم هذه تعوذ من نار جهنم

DURR-FULL:v1p90/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Fire is prepared for anyone whose disbelief is like that of the people being addressed.
DURR-FULL:v1p90/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أعدت للكافرين} قال: أي لمن كان على مثل ما أنتم عليه من الكفر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r1.claim: Qatadah glosses the challenge as inability: if you cannot do it, you will not be able; therefore fear the Fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة فان لن تفعلوا فان لم تطيقوه ولن تطيقوه فاتقوا النار

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the fuel stones are sulfur stones that God created as He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال : ان الحجارة التي سماها الله في القران وقودها الناس والحجارة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the stones as black sulfur stones in Hell, with which people are punished alongside the Fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة فاما الحجارة فهي حجارة في النار من كبريت اسود يعذبون به مع النار

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r4.claim: Mujahid describes the sulfur stones as more foul-smelling than carrion.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة قال : حجارة انتن من الجيفة - من كبريت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r5.speaker: محمد بن علي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r5.claim: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali is also reported to say that the stones are sulfur.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي قال : حجارة من كبريت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r6.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r6.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says the stones are harder and larger than ordinary stones.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن عمرو بن دينار فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة قال حجارة اصلب من هذه الحجارة واعظم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Fire is prepared for those who share the addressees' kind of disbelief.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p64#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : اعدت للكافرين اي لمن كان على مثل ما انتم عليه من الكفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r1.claim: If they cannot produce a comparable surah, even after claiming success and consulting their witnesses, their denial defies the divinely supported Messenger and warrants fear of punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r1.anchor: أي فإن لم تأتوا بسورة أو أتيتم بما زعمتم أنه سورة ولم يستطع ذلك شهداؤكم على التفسيرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r2.claim: The object of “do” is omitted and supplied from context: bringing a surah like the Qur’an; Ibn Ashur defers comparison with the ellipsis at 5:67.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r2.anchor: ومفعول { تفعلوا } محذوف يدل عليه السياق أي فإن لم تفعلوا ذلك أي الإتيان بسورة مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r3.claim: Although failure was expected, conditional in presents it as unlikely to encourage a sincere attempt, exhaust excuses, and draw opponents toward fair-minded debate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r3.anchor: وجيء بإن الشرطية التي الأصل فيها عدم القطع مع أن عدم فعلهم هو الأرجح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r4.claim: The progression moves from inviting a surah, to asking them to consider possible failure, to declaring their inability, alternating conciliatory encouragement with warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r4.anchor: كأن المتحدي يتدبر في شأنهم ، ويزن أمرهم فيقول أولا ائتوا بسورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r5.claim: Sibawayh distinguishes lā as negating the present and lan as negating the future.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r5.anchor: ولهذا قال سيبويه لا لنفي يفعل ، ولن لنفي سيفعل فقد قال الخليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r6.speaker: الخليل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r6.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes lan as a contraction of negative lā and the future particle an; Ibn Ashur calls this a good account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r6.anchor: فقد قال الخليل إن لن حرف مختزل من لا النافية وأن الاستقبالية وهو رأي حسن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says lan conveys permanent negation, literally or figuratively as emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري بإفادتها التأبيد حقيقة أو مجازا وهو التأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r8.claim: An unbounded future negation generally covers all future times; Ibn Ashur’s survey finds lan used for emphatic or permanent negation and rejects grammarians who deny that force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342/r8.anchor: وقد استقريت مواقعها في القرآن وكلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r1.claim: The prediction is miraculous because the challenge should have intensified opposition, yet no contemporary opponent produced a rival despite abundant motives, eloquent talent, and public opportunities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r1.anchor: { ولن تفعلوا } من أكبر معجزات القرآن فإنها معجزة من جهتين : الأولى أنها أثبتت أنهم لم يعارضوا لأن ذلك أبعث لهم على المعارضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r2.claim: It is also a continuing prophecy: neither the challenged Arabs nor later generations have produced a successful counter to the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r2.anchor: الثانية أنه أخبر بأنهم لا يأتون بذلك في المستقبل فما أتى أحد منهم ولا ممن خلفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r3.speaker: ابن العلج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Alj is cited for treating إن and لم as competing to govern the same verb; Ibn Ashur says their meanings differ, so this is not the case here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r3.anchor: كما توهمه ابن العلج أحد نحاة الأندلس نسبه إليه في ( التصريح على التوضيح )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r4.claim: The first تفعلوا is jussive under لم: إن governs the condition after the verb has already been construed as negated by لم.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r4.anchor: لأن ( إن ) الشرطية دخلت على الفعل بعد اعتباره منفيا فيكون معنى الشرط متسلطا على ( لم ) وفعلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r5.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi’s works support allowing two particles to compete for one complement when their semantic demands agree.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r5.anchor: وقد أخذ جوازه من كلام أبي علي الفارسي في ( المسائل الدمشقيات ) ومن كتاب ( التذكرة ) له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r6.speaker: الراجز
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r6.claim: A rajaz line pairing the two forms of ka-anna is cited as evidence for particle competition; the poet is unnamed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p342#2/r6.anchor: ومن كتاب ( التذكرة ) له أنه جعل قول الراجز :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r1.claim: “Fear the Fire” stands for omitted conclusions: recognize that Muhammad is truthful, accept God’s oneness and the revelation, and fear punishment if disobedient; recognizing the Messenger entails belief in resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r1.anchor: لدلالته عليه وإيذانه به وهو إيجاز بديع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r2.claim: The compact verb تفعلوا encompasses the challenge’s special conditions—matching the Qur’an and enlisting witnesses—more efficiently than the simpler “bring” in Joseph 12:59–60.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r2.anchor: لأن في لفظ { تفعلوا } هنا من الإيجاز ما ليس مثله في الآية الأخرى إذ الإتيان المتحدى به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r3.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd names the material burned as fuel; Ibn Ashur says this is required here because the verse means fuel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r3.anchor: والوقود بفتح الواو اسم لما يوقد به ، وبالضم مصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya records both vowelings for the meanings of firewood and verbal noun; an unnamed view reverses the usual assignment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية حكي الضم والفتح في كل من الحطب والمصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r5.claim: The usual pattern faʿūl names what an action is done with; seven exceptional forms occur as verbal nouns, including waqūd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r5.anchor: وقياس فعول بفتح الفاء أنه اسم لما يفعل به كالوضوء والحنوط والسعوط والوجور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r6.claim: A noncanonical ḍamma reading is construed either as a verbal noun or by ellipsis, “those whose fuel is people and stones.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p343/r6.anchor: وقريء بالضم في الشاذ وذلك على اعتبار الضم مصدرا أو على حذف مضاف أي ذوو وقودها الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r1.claim: Al-nās refers to the unbelieving class by customary generic definiteness; it may instead be definite by prior covenant, since other verses identify the people as polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r1.anchor: والناس أريد به صنف منهم وهم الكافرون فتعريفه تعريف الاستغراق العرفي ويجوز أن يكون تعريف العهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r2.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r2.claim: The plural ḥijāra is an unusual, nonanalogical plural of ḥajar; Sibawayh compares its feminine ending to forms such as baʿūla and fuʿūla.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r2.anchor: قال سيبويه كما ألحقوها بالبعولة والفحولة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r3.speaker: أبو الهيثم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r3.claim: Abu al-Haytham says Arabs add tāʾ marbūṭa to plurals on faʿāl or faʿūl to ease pausing after the final consonant and long vowel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r3.anchor: وعن أبي الهيثم أن العرب تدخل الهاء في كل جمع على فعال أو فعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r4.claim: Stones serve as the Fire’s fuel, burning more intensely and slowly extinguishing; the stones include the idols, as stated explicitly at 21:98.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r4.anchor: ومعنى وقودها الحجارة أن الحجر جعل لها مكان الحطب لأنه إذا اشتعل صار أشد إحراقا وأبطأ انطفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r5.claim: The warning indirectly threatens the audience with becoming fuel themselves: “people” signals worshippers, while “stones” signals their idols, through two levels of inference.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r5.anchor: وفي هذه الآية تعريض بتهديد المخاطبين والمعنى المعرض به فاحذروا أن تكونوا أنتم وما عبدتم وقود النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r6.claim: Casting idols into Hell humiliates them and exposes their worshippers’ error; their former source of pride and hoped-for rescue becomes a cause of punishment and lasting regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p344/r6.anchor: وحكمة إلقاء حجارة الأصنام في النار مع أنها لا تظهر فيها حكمة الجزاء أن ذلك تحقير لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.claim: “Prepared for the unbelievers” is an independent predication, not a coordinated second modifier; its independent force heightens terror and implies preparation for the interlocutors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.anchor: استئناف لم يعطف لقصد التنبيه على أنه مقصود بالخبرية لأنه لو عطف لأوهم العطف أنه صفة ثانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability is uniquely established by mass transmission: Arabs perceived it directly, later audiences through transmission, and Arabic specialists can also assess it directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.anchor: فأما القرآن فإعجازه ثبت بالتواتر النقلي أدرك معجزته العرب بالحس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.claim: The challenge uses the Arabs’ own letters, words, and rhetorical styles; their inability to match the Qur’an despite talent, collaboration, and powerful motives shows its eloquence exceeds human capacity and confirms revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.anchor: وهذا هو رأي جمهور أهل السنة والمعتزلة وأعيان الأشاعرة مثل أبي بكر الباقلاني وعبد القاهر الجرجاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.claim: The Arab tribes’ voluntary, rapid acceptance after Mecca’s conquest is further evidence: once Quraysh’s opposition fell, many strong tribes had no reason to capitulate unless they were already convinced and only pride had delayed them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.anchor: ذلك الدليل هو إسلام جميع قبائل العرب وتعاقبهم في الوفادة بعد فتح مكة فإنهم كانوا مقتدين بقريش في المعارضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.claim: The words “you will never do it” remain a miracle across centuries because no one among the original challengers or their successors has opposed the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.anchor: فإنها قد مرت عليها العصور والقرون وماصدقها واضح إذ لم تقع المعارضة من أحد من المخاطبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.claim: Non-Arabs can know the miracle by proof even without the Arabs’ immediate linguistic perception; learning Arabic language and literary style lets them approach the same direct appreciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.anchor: فيكون الإعجاز للعرب بالبداهة ولمن جاء بعدهم بالاستدلال والبرهان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r1.claim: The challengers' universal failure to produce anything like the Qur'an is transmitted by repeated challenge verses and their silence despite strong motives to answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r1.anchor: فعجز جميع المتحدين عن الإتيان بمثل القرآن أمر متواتر بتواتر هذه الآيات بينهم وسكوتهم عن المعارضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r2.speaker: طائفة قليلة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r2.claim: A small group explains the failure by God's diverting the challengers, either stripping their ability or their desire, so the proof would be public to all Arabs; this view is called ṣarfah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r2.anchor: فذهبت طائفة قليلة إلى تعليله بأن الله صرفهم عن معارضة القرآن فسلبهم المقدرة أو سلبهم الداعي ، لتقوم الحجة عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r3.claim: Ṣarfah is named with the form of a one-time act to signal a special diversion, and the term became a conventional name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r3.anchor: ويعرف هذا القول بالصرفة كما في المواقف للعضد والمقاصد للتفتزاني ولعلها بفتح الصاد وسكون الراء وهي مرة من الصرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r4.claim: Reports differ on who held ṣarfah: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ attributes it only to al-Ashʿarī; al-Mawāqif lists al-Naẓẓām, al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā, and al-Iṣfarāyīnī; Ibn Ḥazm states it, while al-Maqāṣid's commentary attributes it to many Muʿtazilites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r4.anchor: ولم ينسبوا هذا القول إلا إلى الأشعري فيما حكاه أبو الفضل عياض في الشفاء وإلى النظام والشريف المرتضى وأبي إسحاق الاسفرائيني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r5.speaker: جمهرة أهل العلم والتحقيق
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r5.claim: The majority of scholars and investigators, the Ashʿarī imams, Imam al-Ḥaramayn, al-Jāḥiẓ, and Arabic scholars explain the failure by the Qur'an's eloquence surpassing Arab rhetoricians; Ibn ʿĀshūr adopts this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r5.anchor: وأما الذي عليه جمهرة أهل العلم والتحقيق واقتصر عليه أيمة الأشعرية وإمام الحرمين وعليه الجاحظ وأهل العربية كما في المواقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr's argument for eloquence as the reason is that legal rulings may be abrogated while their verses remain recited and written, which is justified by their eloquence; he cites the testament verse in al-Māʾida.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r6.anchor: وقد بدا لي دليل قوي على هذا وهو بقاء الآيات التي نسخ حكمها وبقيت متلوة من القرآن ومكتوبة في المصاحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r7.claim: The challenge specifies a whole sūra, even a short one, because eloquence can depend on the full composition: openings and endings, transitions, return to a theme, separation, concision, expansion, digression, and interruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r7.anchor: وإنما وقع التحدي بسورة أي وإن كانت قصيرة دون أن يتحداهم بعدد من الآيات لأن من أفانين البلاغة ما مرجعه إلى مجموع نظم الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r8.speaker: شرف الدين الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r8.claim: Al-Ṭībī likewise explains the challenge to a sūra, rather than a fixed number of verses, through the rhetorical force of the whole composition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r8.anchor: وقد جعل شرف الدين الطيبي هذا هو الوجه لإيقاع التحدي بسورة دون أن يجعل بعدد من الآيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr organizes the Qur'an's inimitability into three aspects: the highest Arabic eloquence with abundant subtle meanings beyond ordinary lexical usage; novel but Arabic-permitted styles; and wisdom and indications of rational and scientific truths beyond human knowledge at revelation and afterward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r9.anchor: فنرى ملاك وجوه الإعجاز راجعا إلى ثلاث جهات : الجهة الأولى : بلوغه الغاية القصوى مما يمكن أن يبلغه الكلام العربي البليغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r10.claim: He says theologians such as al-Bāqillānī and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ overlooked the third aspect, the Qur'an's wisdom and disclosure of rational and scientific truths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r10.anchor: وهذه الجهة أغفلها المتكلمون في إعجاز القرآن من علمائنا مثل أبي بكر الباقلاني والقاضي عياض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r11.speaker: كثير من العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r11.claim: Many scholars count a fourth aspect: reports of unseen matters from the Knower of the unseen, including past peoples' histories that only a rare scripture scholar would know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r11.anchor: وقد عد كثير من العلماء من وجوه إعجاز القرآن ما يعد جهة رابعة هي ما انطوى عليه من الأخبار عن المغيبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r12.speaker: القاضي عياض
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r12.claim: In al-Shifāʾ, Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats reports of earlier peoples as a fourth aspect: this challenged the unlettered Arabs but not the People of the Book, and is compelling to fair-minded readers of the Prophet's background, not deniers who alleged a human taught him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p103/r12.anchor: وخاص ثبوت إعجازه بأهل الإنصاف من الناظرين في نشأة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وأحواله ، وليس معجزا للمكابرين فقد قالوا إنما يعلمه بشر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r1.claim: The Prophet repeatedly challenged and reproached the opponents; none met the challenge, and Musaylima’s attempt exposed its pretension.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r1.anchor: فما فعلوا ولا قدروا ، ومن تعاطى ذلك من سخفائهم كمسيلمة كشف عواره لجميعهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r2.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r2.claim: On hearing the verse about God commanding justice and beneficence, al-Walid praised its sweetness and fruitfulness and said it was not human speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r2.anchor: ولما سمع الوليد بن المغيرة قوله تعالى : ) إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان ( الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda recounts that a Bedouin prostrated on hearing “Proclaim what you are commanded,” saying he prostrated for its eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r3.anchor: وذكر أبو عبيدة أن أعرابيا سمع رجلا يقرأ فاصدع بما تؤمر فسجد وقال : سجدت لفصاحته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r4.claim: In “proclaim what you are commanded,” ṣdaʿ conveys public declaration and courage, while “what you are commanded” is concise and comprehensive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r4.anchor: وكان موضع التأثير في هذه الجملة هو كلمة اصدع في إبانتها عن الدعوة والجهر بها والشجاعة فيها ، وكلمة بما تؤمر في إيجازها وجمعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda also recounts that another listener, hearing Joseph’s brothers confide together, said no created being could produce such speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r5.anchor: وذكر أبو عبيدة أن أعرابيا سمع رجلا يقرأ فاصدع بما تؤمر فسجد وقال : سجدت لفصاحته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r6.claim: The Qur’an’s challenge and the Arabs’ inability to answer are known in general by necessity; rhetoricians analyze the details.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r6.anchor: وكون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تحدى به وأن العرب عجزوا عن معارضته مما علم بالضرورة إجمالا وتصدى أهل علم البلاغة لتفصيله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r7.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r7.claim: Al-Sakkaki says the Qur’an’s inimitability is perceived but cannot itself be described; its apprehension rests on rhetorical taste.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r7.anchor: قال السكاكي في المفتاح : واعلم أن شأن الإعجاز عجيب يدرك ولا يمكن وصفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r8.speaker: التفتازاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r8.claim: Al-Taftazani compares inimitability to perceived meter or beauty: taste detects subtle verbal excellences that ordinary description cannot specify.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r8.anchor: قال التفتزاني يعني أن كل ما ندركه بعقولنا ففي غالب الأمر نتمكن من التعبير عنه ، والإعجاز ليس كذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r9.claim: Rhetorical taste is a faculty for hidden verbal beauties; it may be innate or developed through sustained study of semantics and eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r9.anchor: وليس مدرك الإعجاز عند المصنف سوى الذوق وهو قوة إدراكية لها اختصاص بإدراك لطائف الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the Muʿtazilī theory of ṣarfa, in which God diverted the Arabs and removed their ability to imitate the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r10.anchor: لا كما ذهب إليه النظام وجمع من المعنزلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r11.claim: He rejects the view that inimitability lies in a style unlike Arabic poetry, oratory, and letters, including distinctive verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r11.anchor: ولا كما ذهب إليه جماعة من أن إعجازه بمخالفة أسلوبه لأساليب كلامهم من الأشعار والخطب والرسائل لا سيما في المقاطع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r12.speaker: السيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r12.claim: Al-Sayyid notes that this style theory also points to distinctive sura openings and verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r12.anchor: قال السيد لا سيما في مطالع السور ومقاطع الآي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r13.claim: He rejects explanations based on freedom from contradiction despite length or reports of unseen events, saying such accounts fail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r13.anchor: أو بسلامته من التناقض قال السيد مع طوله جدا أو باشتماله على الإخبار بالمغيبات والكل فاسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r14.speaker: السيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r14.claim: Al-Sayyid counts five explanations of inimitability and reconciles its indescribable nature with the possibility of analyzing rhetorical features.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p106/r14.anchor: وقال السيد : الجرجاني فهذه أقوال خمسة في وجه الإعجاز لا سادس لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.claim: In in lam tafʿalū, in precedes lam because lam tafʿalū means they left the act undone; in does not affect the equivalent of a past-tense verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r18.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فإن لم تفعلوا، دخلت «إن» على لم لأن لم تفعلوا معناه تركتم الفعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.claim: Tafʿalū is jussive after lam; lam takes the jussive because, like prohibitive lā, it negates, deleting the verb’s ending as lā deletes a noun’s tanwin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p106#2/r19.anchor: وتفعلوا جزم ب لم، وجزمت ب لم لأنها أشبهت «لا» في التبرية في أنهما ينفيان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r1.claim: Lan normally makes a verb subjunctive, though Abu Ubayda reports that some Arabs use it jussively; the Nābigha verse and Ibn Umar dream report illustrate the usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r1.anchor: ومن العرب من تجزم بها، ذكره أبو عبيدة، ومنه بيت النابغة على بعض الروايات:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r2.claim: The categorical prediction stirs their resolve, making their later inability more striking, and reports unseen knowledge before it occurred.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r2.anchor: وفي قوله: لن تفعلوا إثارة لهممهم وتحريك لنفوسهم، ليكون عجزهم بعد ذلك أبدع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r3.claim: “Guard yourselves from the Fire” is a command to believe and obey God, phrased as a warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فاتقوا النار، أمر بالإيمان وطاعة الله خرج في هذه الألفاظ المحذرة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r4.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن، مجاهد، طلحة بن مصرف، أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r4.claim: The majority read waqūduhā with fatḥa; al-Hasan, Mujahid, Talha ibn Musarrif, and Abu Haywa use ḍamma throughout the Qur’an, except Talha exempts its occurrence in al-Buruj.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف وأبو حيوة: «وقودها» بضم الواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r5.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd means fuel or firewood; with ḍamma it means kindling, though both forms are attested for both senses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r5.anchor: وبفتح الواو هو الحطب وبضمها هو المصدر، وقد حكيا جميعا في الحطب وقد حكيا في المصدر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r6.speaker: ابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r6.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the ḍamma reading by an omitted noun, “possessor of fuel,” since a verbal noun cannot be people; fatḥa for the verbal noun is anomalous, while ḍamma is the normal pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r6.anchor: قال ابن جني: «من قرأ بضم الواو فهو على حذف مضاف تقديره ذو وقودها، لأن الوقود بالضم مصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r7.claim: “People” is grammatically general but specifically means those decreed to enter the Fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r7.anchor: وقوله: الناس عموم معناه الخصوص فيمن سبق عليه القضاء بدخولها.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r8.claim: Ibn Masud says the stones are sulfur; they add five torments: quick ignition, foul smell, abundant smoke, clinging to bodies, and intense heat when heated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود في الحجارة أنها حجارة الكبريت وخصت بذلك لأنها تزيد على جميع الأحجار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r9.claim: “Prepared” refutes those who say the Fire has not yet been created; Ibn Atiyya names the Andalusian Mundhir ibn Said al-Baluti as having fallen into that view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r9.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: أعدت رد على من قال: إن النار لم تخلق حتى الآن، وهو القول الذي سقط فيه منذر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r10.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r10.claim: Some interpreters say the Fire described with stones is specifically for unbelievers, while sinners have another Fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r10.anchor: وذهب بعض المتأولين إلى أن هذه النار المخصصة بالحجارة هي نار الكافرين خاصة، وأن غيرها هي للعصاة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r11.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r11.claim: The majority take this as the Fire generally; mentioning unbelievers intensifies the warning because the addressees act in unbelief, without excluding others from entering it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p107/r11.anchor: وقال الجمهور: بل الإشارة إلى جميع النار لا إلى نار مخصوصة، وإنما ذكر الكافرين ليحصل المخاطبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p108/r1.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p108/r1.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads “Allah prepared it for the unbelievers,” adding Allah as the subject and changing the verb form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p108/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: «أعدها الله للكافرين»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r1.claim: An omitted premise is understood: after the preceding challenge went unanswered, the discourse continues, ‘if you do not.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r1.anchor: في هذه الآية مضمر مقدر يقتضي الكلام تقديمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r2.claim: The prediction that they would never produce its like, which came true, is strong evidence for the Prophet’s prophethood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r2.anchor: أعظم دلالة على صحة نبوة نبينا لأنه أخبر أنهم لا يفعلون ولم يفعلوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r3.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd means firewood; with ḍamma it means the act or flame of kindling, as with wuḍūʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r3.anchor: والوقود بفتح الواو الحطب وبضمها التوقد كالوضوء بالفتح الماء وبالضم المصدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatāda read waqūd with ḍamma on the wāw.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن و قتادة وقودها بضم الواو والاختيار الفتح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī prefers the reading with fatḥa on the wāw.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن و قتادة وقودها بضم الواو والاختيار الفتح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r6.claim: People are kindled in the Fire as punishment; the stones convey its force and severity because it burns stones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r6.anchor: والناس أو قدوا فيها بطريق العذاب والحجارة لبيان قوتها وشدتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r7.claim: One interpretation identifies the stones as the idols people worshipped.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الحجارة قولان احدهما أنها أصنامهم التي عبدوها قاله الربيع بن أنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r8.claim: The other interpretation identifies them as sulfur stones, said to be intensely hot when heated and used to punish people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r8.anchor: والثاني أنها حجارة الكبريت وهي أشد الأشياء حرا إذا أحميت يعذبون بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r9.anchor: ومعنى اعدت هيئت وإنما خوفهم بالنار إذا لم يأتوا بمثل القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r10.claim: Their inability to match the Quran after denying it establishes the proof against them; opposition then becomes obstinacy, whose recompense is the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p51/r10.anchor: لأنهم إذا كذبوه وعجزوا عن الاتيان بمثله ثبتت عليهم الحجة وصار الخلاف عنادا وجزاء المعاندين النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r1.claim: Waqud, with fatHa on the waw, means fuel thrown into a fire to kindle it, such as firewood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r1.anchor: أما الوقود، بفتح الواو، فهو ما يلقى في النار لإضرامها كالحطب ونحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links the fire’s fuel imagery to 72:15, where the unjust are firewood for Hell, and 21:98, where worshippers and their idols are fuel for it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r2.anchor: كما قال: {وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا} [الجن: 15] وقال تعالى: {إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the stones as enormous, black, hard, foul-smelling sulfur stones, among the hottest stones when heated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r3.anchor: والمراد بالحجارة هاهنا: هي حجارة الكبريت العظيمة السوداء الصلبة المنتنة، وهي أشد الأحجار حرا إذا حميت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r4.claim: Ibn Masud said the stones are sulfur stones God created in the lowest heaven when He created the heavens and earth, preparing them for disbelievers; Ibn Kathir cites Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who graded the report to the standards of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، في قوله تعالى: {وقودها الناس والحجارة} قال: هي حجارة من كبريت، خلقها الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r5.claim: Al-Suddi, reporting from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and other Companions, says the stones are black sulfur stones in Hell used to torment its inhabitants alongside the fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r5.anchor: وقال السدي في تفسيره، عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r6.claim: Mujahid says the stones are sulfur stones more foul-smelling than carrion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: حجارة من كبريت أنتن من الجيفة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r7.claim: Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali also identifies the stones as sulfur stones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r7.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي: [هي] (8) حجارة من كبريت.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj specifies that they are black sulfur stones in the fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r8.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: حجارة من كبريت أسود في النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r9.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r9.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says the sulfur stones are harder and larger than ordinary stones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r9.anchor: وقال لي عمرو بن دينار: أصلب من هذه الحجارة وأعظم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r10.speaker: فخر الدين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r10.claim: Fakhr al-Din reports and prefers the view that the stones are idols worshipped apart from God, rather than sulfur fuel stones; Ibn Kathir rejects this preference as weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r10.anchor: حكاه القرطبي وفخر الدين ورجحه على الأول؛ قال: لأن أخذ النار في حجارة الكبريت ليس بمنكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir says the idol interpretation is weak: sulfur stones intensify the fire, fire heating stones is observable, and the verse emphasizes the promised fire’s heat and blazing force.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r11.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله ليس بقوي،؛ وذلك أن النار إذا أضرمت بحجارة الكبريت كان ذلك أشد لحرها وأقوى لسعيرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r12.claim: Ibn Kathir cites 17:97 to show how the fire’s intensity is increased whenever it subsides; al-Qurtubi likewise prefers stones that fuel and intensify the blaze because that makes the torment worse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r12.anchor: كما قال: {كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا} [الإسراء: 97] . وهكذا رجح القرطبي أن المراد بها الحجارة التي تسعر بها النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r13.speaker: القرطبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r13.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites a report that every harmful thing is in the Fire; Ibn Kathir says the report is not preserved or known.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r13.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "كل مؤذ في النار" وهذا الحديث ليس بمحفوظ ولا معروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r14.speaker: القرطبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi gives two readings of the harmful-things report: everyone who harms people enters the Fire, or harmful creatures inhabit it and torment its people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p201/r14.anchor: ثم قال القرطبي: وقد فسر بمعنيين، أحدهما: أن كل من آذى الناس دخل النار (2) ، والآخر: كل ما يؤذي فهو في النار يتأذى به أهلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the pronoun in “prepared” most naturally refers to the Fire fueled by people and stones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r1.anchor: الأظهر أن الضمير في {أعدت} عائد إلى النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r2.claim: Ibn Masud also took the pronoun to refer to the stones; Ibn Kathir says this agrees in meaning because the stones and Fire are joined.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r2.anchor: ويحتمل عوده على الحجارة، كما قال ابن مسعود،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r3.claim: The two proposed referents do not conflict, since the Fire and the stones are connected.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r3.anchor: ولا منافاة بين القولين في المعنى؛ لأنهما متلازمان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r4.claim: “Prepared” means made ready and reserved for those who disbelieve in God and His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r4.anchor: و {أعدت} أي: أرصدت وحصلت للكافرين بالله ورسوله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Fire is prepared for people whose disbelief is like that of the addressees; the report comes through Ikrima or Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {أعدت للكافرين} أي: لمن كان على مثل ما أنتم عليه من الكفر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r6.speaker: أئمة السنة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r6.claim: Many Sunni imams infer that Hell already exists because the verse says it has been prepared and made ready.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r6.anchor: وقد استدل كثير من أئمة السنة بهذه الآية على أن النار موجودة الآن لقوله: {أعدت}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r7.claim: As evidence for Hell's present existence, Ibn Kathir cites reports of Paradise and Fire disputing and of Hell asking God for relief from consuming itself, as well as eclipse-prayer and Night Journey reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r7.anchor: وقد وردت أحاديث كثيرة في ذلك منها: "تحاجت الجنة والنار" ومنها: "استأذنت النار ربها فقالت:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r8.claim: Ibn Masud reports hearing a sound; the Prophet said a stone cast from Hell's rim seventy years earlier had just reached its bottom; Muslim records it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r8.anchor: وحديث ابن مسعود سمعنا وجبة فقلنا ما هذه؟ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "هذا حجر ألقي به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Muʿtazila wrongly denied Hell's present existence, and the Andalusian judge Mundhir ibn Saʿid al-Baluti agreed with them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p202/r9.anchor: وقد خالفت المعتزلة بجهلهم في هذا ووافقهم القاضي منذر بن سعيد البلوطي قاضي الأندلس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r1.claim: The Quran is a lasting miracle above earlier prophets’ signs and books: its revelation is continuously transmitted and remains as revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r1.anchor: وفي هذا الحديث فضيلة عظيمة للقرآن المجيد على كل معجزة أعطيها نبي من الأنبياء، وعلى كل كتاب أنزله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r2.claim: The Quranic challenge narrows from the whole Quran to ten surahs and then one surah; the verses declare the challengers unable now and in the future.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r2.anchor: ثم تقاصر معهم إلى عشر سور منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r3.claim: Though Arabs excelled at eloquence and poetry, they could not match the Quran’s concise language, sound knowledge, true reports of the unseen, and just rulings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p20/r3.anchor: لكن جاءهم من الله مالا قبل لأحد من البشرية من الكلام الفصيح البليغ، الوجيز، المحتوي على العلوم الكثيرة الصحيحة النافعة، والأخبار الصادقة عن الغيوب الماضية والآتية، والأحكام العادلة والمحكمة،

JISHUMI:v1p287/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r1.claim: The challenge applies to the Qur’an and portions of it, demonstrating the truth of Muhammad’s prophethood.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r1.anchor: فلذلك صح التحدي بسورة مرة، وبعشر سور مرة، وبكل القرآن مرة

JISHUMI:v1p287/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r2.claim: The surah is revealed as it stands, not composed in ʿUthmān’s time as some claimed; this validates the challenges by one surah, ten, or all of the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن هذه السورة كما هي منزلة لا كما زعم بعضهم أنه نظم أيام عثمان

JISHUMI:v1p287/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r3.claim: The Qur’an is God’s speech and not human speech.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن القرآن كلام الله تعالى، وليس من كلام البشر

JISHUMI:v1p287/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r4.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v1p287/r4.claim: The general reading has waqūduhā with fatḥa on the wāw.

JISHUMI:v1p287/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r5.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p287/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid are reported to read the wāw with ḍamma, which the author rejects as incorrect.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن ومجاهد بضم الواو، وليس بصحيح

JISHUMI:v1p287/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r6.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
JISHUMI:v1p287/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmayr is reported to read waqīduhā, but the author rejects it because Qur’anic reading must be widely transmitted.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r6.anchor: وعن عبيد بن عمير: وقيدها، ولا يجوز القراءة بهما

JISHUMI:v1p287/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r7.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd means fuel or firewood; with ḍamma, it means kindling.

JISHUMI:v1p287/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r8.speaker: ابن الخليل
JISHUMI:v1p287/r8.claim: Fiʿl, iḥdāth, and ījād are near-synonyms; the two vocalizations of fiʿl distinguish verbal noun from noun, as Ibn al-Khalīl explains.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r8.anchor: فالمفتوح المصدر، والمكسور الاسم، هكذا ذكره ابن الخليل

JISHUMI:v1p287/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r9.claim: An act implies its agent is capable; awaiting or ordering acts implies knowledge, and mediation implies that the agent exists and is living.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r9.anchor: الفعل بنفسه يدل على كون فاعله قادرا، وبانتظار أو بانتظام الفعل على كونه عالما

JISHUMI:v1p287/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r10.claim: Ḥijāra is the singular of ḥajar, an irregular formation; the regular plural would be aḥjār.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r10.anchor: والحجارة واحدها حجر، وليس بقياس، فالقياس أحجار

JISHUMI:v1p287/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r11.claim: Iʿdād means preparing something for someone, as in the command to prepare against them.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r11.anchor: والإعداد: مصدر أعد له كذا، أي هيأ، ومنه: (وأعدوا لهم)

JISHUMI:v1p287/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r12.claim: Wa-lan tafʿalū is a parenthetical interruption, as parentheticals can separate a condition from its consequence.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r12.anchor: كما يتصل الاعتراض بين المبتدأ والخبر، وبين الشرط والجزاء

JISHUMI:v1p287/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r13.claim: One grammatical view gives the clause no syntactic position because no governing element acts on it.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r13.anchor: فقيل: لا موضع لها من الإعراب؛ إذ لم يعمل فيها عامل

JISHUMI:v1p287/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p287/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p287/r14.claim: The author illustrates parenthetical clauses with 3:30, where innā lā nuḍīʿu interrupts the sentence and the predicate follows afterward.
JISHUMI:v1p287/r14.anchor: فقوله: (إنا لا نضيع) اعتراض، والخبر: أولئك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r1.claim: If they cannot meet the challenge, the truth of the Messenger becomes clear, so they must believe and fear the prepared punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r1.anchor: لما أرشدهم إلى الجهة التي منها يتعرفون امر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما جاء به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r2.claim: The verse establishes prophethood both by the challenge’s miraculous nature and by foretelling their failure, knowledge of the unseen that belongs only to God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r2.anchor: وفيه دليلان على إثبات النبوة صحة كون المتحدي به معجزا والإخبار بأنهم لن يفعلوا وهو غيب لا يعلمه الا الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r3.claim: Using إن rather than the certainty-marking إذا matches their expectation: before reflection, they trusted their eloquence and regarded failure as uncertain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r3.anchor: ان يساق القول معهم على حسب حسبانهم وطمعهم وان العجز عن المعارضة كان قبل التامل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, إن is sarcastic: like a strong man saying ‘if you defeat me’ while certain he will win, it mocks their confidence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r4.anchor: والثاني ان يتهكم بهم كما يقول الموصوف بالقوة الواثق من نفسه بالغلبة على من يقاويه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r5.claim: Saying ‘do it’ as ‘act’ treats producing a sura as an action and compresses the fuller expression through metonymy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r5.anchor: لأنه فعل من الأفعال تقول أتيت فلانا فيقال لك نعم ما فعلت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r6.claim: The clause ‘and you will never do it’ is parenthetical and has no syntactic position.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r6.anchor: لا محل لها لأنها جملة اعتراضية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r7.claim: لن and لا both negate the future, but لن adds emphasis and intensification.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r7.anchor: لا ولن أختان في نفي المستقبل الا ان في لن توكيدا وتشديدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r8.speaker: الخليل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r8.claim: One reported etymology derives لن from لا أن.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r8.anchor: وهي عند الخليل في إحدى الروايتين عنه أصلها لا أن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r9.speaker: الفراء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains لن as لا whose alif was changed into nūn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p130#3/r9.anchor: وعند الفراء لا أبدلت ألفها نونا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r1.speaker: سيبويه، إحدى الروايتين عن الخليل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r1.claim: Sībawayh, and another account from al-Khalīl, treat لن as an abbreviated particle that emphasizes future negation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r1.anchor: وعند سيبويه وإحدى الروايتين عن الخليل حرف مقتضب لتأكيد نفي المستقبل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r2.claim: If they had produced a rival sura, people would have transmitted it; its absence from transmission, despite many opponents, proves the unseen prediction and thus the miracle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r2.anchor: لأنهم لو عارضوه بشيء لم يمتنع ان يتواصفه الناس ويتناقلوه اذ خفاء مثله فيما عليه مبنى العادة محال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r3.claim: Once inability establishes the Messenger’s truth, persistent refusal to follow him merits Hell; the warning therefore urges them to abandon obstinacy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131/r3.anchor: اذا لم يأتوا بها وتبين عجزهم عن المعارضة صح عندهم صدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.claim: Fear of the Fire is metonymy for abandoning opposition, since that is its consequence; the concise wording magnifies obstinacy and the Fire’s terror.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.anchor: موضعه لأن اتقاء النار لصيقة وضميمه ترك العناد من حيث انه من نتائجه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.claim: The king’s instruction to beware his anger similarly means obey and follow his command; the indirect phrasing is concise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.anchor: ونظيره ان يقول الملك لحشمه أن أردتم الكرامة عندي فاحذروا سخطي يريد فأطيعوني واتبعوا امري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.claim: وقود names what fuels a fire; as a verbal noun it is usually vocalized with ḍamma, though fatḥ is also attested.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.anchor: والوقود ما ترفع به النار واما المصدر فمضموم وقد جاء فيه الفتح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh reports hearing Arabs use وقود as a verbal noun and says the fuel noun is more common; وقود also means firewood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه وسمعنا من العرب من يقول وقدت النار وقودا عاليا ثم قال والوقود أكثر والوقود الحطب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.speaker: عيسى بن عمر الهمداني
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdānī reads وقود with ḍamma, using the verbal noun as the fuel’s name.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر الهمداني بالضم تسمية بالمصدر كما يقال فلان فخر قومه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.claim: The relative clause can describe a fire already known to the audience from People of the Book, the Messenger, or the earlier warning in al-Taḥrīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.anchor: صلة الذي والتي يجب أن تكون قصة معلومة للمخاطب فكيف علم اولئك ان نار الآخرة توقد بالناس والحجارة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r1.claim: The Meccan al-Taḥrīm verse first introduced an indefinite fire of this description; the Medinan verse uses the definite form to refer back to that known fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r1.anchor: تلك الاية نزلت بمكة فعرفوا منها نارا موصوفة بهذه الصفة ثم نزلت هذه بالمدينة مشارا بها إلى ما عرفوه اولا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r2.claim: This Fire is distinctive because people and stones directly fuel it; ordinary fires need fuel first, then burn or heat what is placed in them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r2.anchor: معناه أنها نار ممتازة عن غيرها من النيران بأنها لا تتقد الا بالناس والحجارة وبان غيرها إن أريد إحراق الناس بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r3.claim: Its extreme heat and fierce flame make it ignite even things that do not ordinarily catch fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r3.anchor: تلك اعاذنا الله منها برحمته الواسعة توقد بنفس ما يحرق ويحمي بالنار وبانها لإفراط حرها وشدة ذكائها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r4.claim: Hell contains different fires, including one fueled by people and stones; the indefinite fire in al-Layl supports this reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132/r4.anchor: بل هي نيران شتى منها نار توقد بالناس والحجارة يدل على ذلك تنكيرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.claim: Different kinds of people may have different fires: perhaps jinn and devils fuel a fire for their own kind, as humans fuel one for human unbelievers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.anchor: ولعل لكفار الجن وشياطينهم نارا وقودها الشياطين كما ان لكفرة الإنس نارا وقودها هم جزاء لكل جنس بما يشاكله من العذاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.claim: The idolaters are paired with stones because they carved stone idols and worshipped them or made them partners with God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.anchor: لأنهم قرنوا بها انفسهم في الدنيا حيث نحتوها أصناما وجعلوها لله اندادا أو عبدوها من دونه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.claim: The statement that worshippers and what they worship are Hell’s fuel explains the pairing: ‘you’ corresponds to people and the worshipped objects to stones.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية مفسرة لما نحن فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.claim: Since idolaters trusted their idols as intercessors and protectors, God makes the idols heated punishment beside them, intensifying pain and regret.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.anchor: ولما اعتقد الكفار في حجارتهم المعبودة من دون الله انها الشفعاء والشهداء الذين يستشفعون بهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.claim: This resembles hoarders whose gold and silver are heated in Hell and used to brand them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.anchor: ونحوهم ما يفعله بالكانزين الذين جعلوا ذهبهم وفضتهم عدة وذخيرة فشحوا بها ومنعوها من الحقوق حيث يحمى عليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.claim: The claim that the stones are specifically sulfur is unsupported and abandons the sound, textually corroborated meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.anchor: وقيل هي حجارة الكبريت وهو تخصيص بغير دليل وذهاب عما هو المعنى الصحيح الواقع المشهود له بمعاني التنزيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r1.claim: The Fire has been prepared and set aside as punishment for unbelievers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r2.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads أعتدت, from عتاد, meaning prepared equipment or provision.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p133/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله أعتدت من العتاد بمعنى العدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r8.claim: With fatḥa, waqūd means fuel or firewood; with ḍamma, wuqūd means kindling or the act of burning. The stones are black sulfur.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r8.anchor: الوقود بالفتح الحطب , والوقود بالضم التوقد , والحجارة من كبريت أسود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās say the people are punished with stones alongside the fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r9.anchor: يعذبون فيها بالحجارة مع النار , التي وقودها الناس , وهذا قول ابن مسعود وابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r10.claim: Another view makes the stones fuel along with people, magnifying the fire as one that burns stones as well as people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r10.anchor: أن الحجارة وقود النار مع الناس , ذكر ذلك تعظيما للنار , كأنها تحرق الحجارة مع إحراقها الناس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r11.claim: One view says the same fire also holds other people liable to punishment, whose penalties differ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r11.anchor: فهي معدة لغيرهم من مستحقي العذاب من غير الكافرين , وهي نار واحدة , وإنما يتفاوت عقابهم فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r12.claim: The alternative is that this fire is only for disbelievers, with a different fire for other people liable to punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p84/r12.anchor: أن هذه النار معدة للكافرين خاصة , ولغيرهم من مستحقي العذاب نار غيرها

MUQATIL:2:24/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:24/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:24/r1.claim: Muqatil reads the challenge as requiring a surah like the Quran: if they fail, they will never produce one; he notes fronting in the wording.
MUQATIL:2:24/r1.anchor: { فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا } ، يعنى تجيئوا به، فيها تقديم تقديمها،

MUQATIL:2:24/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:24/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:24/r2.claim: The stones are sulfur-like stones beneath the second earth, put around the damned people's necks; they burn most of the day and their blaze scorches faces, as in 39:24.
MUQATIL:2:24/r2.anchor: وتلك الحجارة تحت الأرض الثانية مثل الكبريت تجعل فى أعناقهم إذا اشتعلت فيها النار

MUQATIL:2:24/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:24/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:24/r3.claim: God warns the disbelievers with the fire, but they dismiss its description by asking how stones can be fuel; believers are frightened by the warning.
MUQATIL:2:24/r3.anchor: فلم يخافوا، فقالوا من تكذيبهم: هذه النار وقودها الناس، فما بال الحجارة، فرق المؤمنون عند التخويف.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.claim: If they cannot answer the challenge, the Prophet’s truth is clear; they should believe rather than persist in denial and incur punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.anchor: فإذا لم تعارضوه وبان عجزكم ووجب تصديقه فآمنوا وخافوا العذاب المعد لمن كذب وعاند

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.claim: The inimitable challenge establishes prophethood, and predicting they will never answer it is unseen knowledge known only to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.anchor: وفيه دليلا على إثبات النبوة صحة كون المتحدى به معجزا والاخبار بأنهم لن يفعلوا وهو غيب لا يعلمه إلا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.claim: Because inability seemed doubtful to eloquent opponents, إن expresses their uncertainty rather than إذا, which signals certainty.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.anchor: لما كان العجز عن المعارضة قبل التأمل كالمشكوك فيه لديهم لا تكالهم على فصاحتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.claim: إن is the conditional particle for doubt, unlike إذا for certainty, matching the opponents’ expectation before reflection.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.anchor: فجئ بان الذى للشك دون إذا الذي للوجوب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.claim: The concise فعل replaces the longer phrase bring a sūra like it, functioning as metonymic abbreviation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.anchor: وعبر عن الاتيان بالفعل لأنه فعل من الأفعال والفائدة فيه أنه جار مجرى الكناية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.claim: ولن تفعلوا is a parenthetical with no syntactic position; it cuts off the hesitation suggested by the conditional.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.anchor: ولا محل لقوله ولن تفعلوا لأنها جملة اعتراضية وحسن هذا الاعتراض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.claim: Al-Khalil derives لن from لا أن.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ says لن is لا with its alif changed to nūn.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.anchor: وعند الفراء لا أبدلت الفها نونا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.speaker: سيبويه
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.claim: Sibawayh calls لن a particle emphasizing future negation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.anchor: وعند سيبويه حرف موضع لتأكيد نفى المستقبل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.claim: The prediction is miraculous because any successful counter would have become famous, especially given the many critics and few defenders.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.anchor: لأنهم لو عارضوه بشئ لاشتهر فكيف والطاعنون فيه اكثر عددا من الذابين عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.claim: Failure to produce a comparable sūra establishes the Messenger’s truth; if they then refuse submission, they deserve the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.anchor: إذا لم يأتوا بها وتبين عجزهم عن المعارضة صح عندهم صدق الرسول

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r12.claim: Fear the Fire stands metonymically for abandoning obstinacy, since leaving denial is the means of avoiding punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r12.anchor: فوضع فاتقوا النار موضعه لأن اتقاء النار سبب ترك العناد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r13.claim: وقود means what feeds a fire, namely firewood; as a verbal noun it is usually with ḍamma, though fatḥ is also attested.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r13.anchor: والوقود ما ترفع به النار يعنى الحطب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r14.claim: The relative clause assumes the audience knows this Fire, perhaps from the People of the Book, the Messenger, or the earlier Meccan verse 66:6.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r14.anchor: وصلة الذى والتى يجب أن تكون معلوما للمخاطب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r15.claim: The audience may have heard of the Fire from the People of the Book, the Messenger, or the earlier Meccan warning in 66:6; the definite wording recalls that prior disclosure.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r15.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكونوا سمعوا من أهل الكتاب أو من رسول الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r16.claim: The Fire is distinctive because it burns people and stones; sulfur stones burn intensely, cool slowly, smell foul, and cling to the body.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r16.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى وقودها الناس والحجارة أنها نار ممتازة عن غيرها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r17.claim: Alternatively, the stones are idols; pairing idolaters with the objects they worship increases their regret because they made them partners of God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r17.anchor: أو الأصنام المعبودة فهى أشد تحسيرا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r18.claim: The pairing recalls 21:98, which calls the people and what they worship besides God fuel for Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r18.anchor: ﴿ إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله ﴾ حصب جهنم أى حطبها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r19.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r19.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r19.claim: The Fire’s having been prepared indicates that it is created.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r19.anchor: هيئت لهم فيه دليل على أن النار مخلوقة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r20.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r20.speaker: جهم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r20.claim: The author rejects Jahm’s view that the Fire is uncreated, taking its preparation as evidence that it is created.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r20.anchor: دليل على أن النار مخلوقة خلافا لما يقوله جهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r21.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r21.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r21.claim: God pairs encouragement with warning to motivate deeds that bring nearness and deter harmful conduct.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p28#2/r21.anchor: سنة الله فى كتابه أن يذكر الترغيب مع الترهيب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r1.claim: The challenge concerns the past attempt and future inability; on this reading the pause at صادقين is complete.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r1.anchor: يعني فيما مضى { ولن تفعلوا } أي تطيقوا ذلك فيما يأتي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r2.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r2.claim: They construe the challenge as continuing through ولن تفعلوا, followed by if you fail, then fear the Fire; صادقين is not a complete pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r2.anchor: وقال جماعة من المفسرين: معنى الآية وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين ولن تفعلوا،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r3.claim: إن is non-governing here, so it can precede لم as it can a past verb; the phrase means if you leave the act undone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r3.anchor: فالجواب أن «إن» ها هنا غير عاملة في اللفظ، فدخلت على «لم» كما تدخل على الماضي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r4.claim: The usual form has نصب after لن, but some Arabs use لن with jussive; Abu Ubayda cites the poet al-Nābigha for this dialect.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r4.anchor: ومن العرب من يجزم بها، ذكره أبو عبيدة ومنه بيت النابغة:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r5.claim: Ibn Umar’s dream report has the phrase لن ترع, illustrating the dialect that uses jussive after لن.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r5.anchor: وفي حديث ابن عمر حين ذهب به إلى النار في منامه: فقيل لي «لن ترع».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r6.claim: The prediction stirs their resolve so that their eventual inability will be more striking, and reports unseen knowledge before it occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: «ولن تفعلوا» إثارة لهممهم، وتحريك لنفوسهم ليكون عجزهم بعد ذلك أبدع،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r7.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r7.claim: The prediction establishes that the Qur’an is true and rebuts their claims that it is false, fabricated, magic, poetry, or tales of old, since they cannot produce a comparable sūra.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r7.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: «ولن تفعلوا» توقيفا لهم على أنه الحق،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r8.claim: Fear the Fire is the response to failure, by believing the Prophet and obeying God; the commentary does not repeat its earlier explanation of taqwā.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r8.anchor: وقوله: { فاتقوا النار } جواب «فإن لم تفعلوا» أي اتقوا النار بتصديق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وطاعة الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r9.claim: The dialects of Tamīm and Asad are said to pronounce the expression فتقوا النار.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r9.anchor: ويقال: إن لغة تميم وأسد «فتقوا النار».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r10.claim: النار is the object and التي its adjective; التي is a definite, feminine relative pronoun that requires a relative clause and cannot lose its article to become indefinite.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r11.claim: The commentary lists three dual forms and five plural forms for the feminine relative pronoun, including the Qur’anic form اللاتي.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24/r11.anchor: وفي تثنيتها ثلاث لغات أيضا: اللتان واللتا بحذف النون واللتان بتشديد النون.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.claim: The source lists plural forms اللاتي, اللات, اللواتي, اللوات, and اللوا; Ibn al-Shajarī adds اللائي, اللاء, and اللا, and gives collective plurals اللواتي and اللوائي.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r1.anchor: وزاد ابن الشجري: اللائي بالهمز وإثبات الياء. واللاء بكسر الهمزة وحذف الياء. واللا بحذف الهمزة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.claim: Al-Jawharī gives اللتيا as the diminutive of التي, supported by a rajaz line.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r2.anchor: قال الجوهري: وتصغير التي اللتيا بالفتح والتشديد قال الراجز:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.claim: Although vocative particles do not normally precede a definite noun, one poet says يا التي, apparently by analogy with يا الله because its article never separates from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r3.anchor: وبعض الشعراء أدخل على «التي» حرف النداء، وحروف النداء لا تدخل على ما فيه الألف واللام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.claim: The phrase اللتيا والتي is used as a name for a calamity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r4.anchor: ويقال: وقع فلان في اللتيا والتي وهما اسمان من أسماء الداهية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r5.claim: With fatḥa, وقود means fuel or firewood; with ḍamma, it means the act of burning.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r6.claim: الناس is general in wording but specifically refers to those decreed to serve as fuel for the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r6.anchor: و «الناس» عموم، ومعناه الخصوص فيمن سبق عليه القضاء أنه يكون حطبا لها أجارنا الله منها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud and al-Farrāʾ identify the stones as black sulfur stones, singled out for their especially severe burning and punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود والفراء وخصت بذلك لأنها تزيد على جميع الأحجار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r8.claim: The sulfur stones intensify punishment through rapid ignition, foul smell, abundant smoke, strong adhesion to bodies, and great heat when heated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r8.anchor: لأنها تزيد على جميع الأحجار بخمسة أنواع من العذاب: سرعة الاتقاد، نتن الرائحة، كثرة الدخان،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r9.claim: Mentioning people and stones as fuel does not exclude jinn and devils, whom the Qur’an places in the Fire elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r9.anchor: وليس في قوله تعالى: { وقودها الناس والحجارة } دليل على أن ليس فيها غير الناس والحجارة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes the stones as idols, citing 21:98; on this reading their mention magnifies the Fire because it consumes stones as well as people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالحجارة الأصنام لقوله تعالى: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r11.claim: On the first interpretation, people are punished by both the Fire and the stones; on the idol interpretation, people and idols fuel the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r11.anchor: وعلى التأويل الأول يكونون معذبين بالنار والحجارة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r12.claim: A Prophetic report says every harmful thing is in the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r12.anchor: وقد جاء الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " كل مؤذ في النار "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r13.claim: One explanation is that everyone who harmed people in worldly life is punished by God with Fire in the Hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r13.anchor: أحدهما: أن كل من آذى الناس في الدنيا عذبه الله في الآخرة بالنار.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r14.claim: Another explanation is that harmful worldly creatures, such as predators and vermin, are in the Fire to punish its inhabitants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r14.anchor: الثاني: أن كل ما يؤذي الناس في الدنيا من السباع والهوام وغيرها في النار معد لعقوبة أهل النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r15.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r15.claim: Some exegetes say this Fire specifically fueled by stones is the Fire of the unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#2/r15.anchor: وذهب بعض أهل التأويل إلى أن هذه النار المخصوصة بالحجارة هي نار الكافرين خاصة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.claim: Abbas asked whether Abu Talib’s protection and support benefited him; the Prophet said it did, moving him from the deepest Fire to a shallow part, and without him he would be in its lowest depth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r1.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب قال: قلت: يا رسول الله،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r2.claim: وقودها is the subject, الناس its predicate, and الحجارة is coordinated with الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
