QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujāhid, and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read وقودها with a ḍamma on the wāw.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف: «وقودها» بضم الواو.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r4.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reads وقيدها with qāf.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.speaker: الكسائي والأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash distinguish open wāw for fuel from ḍamma for burning, and list forms of the verb meaning that the Fire burned or was kindled.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r5.anchor: قال الكسائي والأخفش: الوقود بفتح الواو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.claim: Given the distinction between fuel and burning, al-Naḥḥās says only the fatḥa reading should be read here, while noting al-Akhfash’s report that some Arabs use both forms for fuel and verbal noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r6.anchor: قال النحاس: يجب على هذا ألا يقرأ إلا «وقودها» بفتح الواو لأن المعنى حطبها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says fatḥa is the more common form, by analogy with الوضوء for water and الوضوء for the act of ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: وذهب إلى أن الأول أكثر، قال: كما أن الوضوء الماء، والوضوء المصدر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r8.claim: Although the wording appears to reserve the Fire for unbelievers, warnings for sinners and established intercession reports show that others can enter it too.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أعدت للكافرين } ظاهره أن غير الكافرين لا يدخلها وليس كذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r9.claim: The verse supports the orthodox position that the Fire already exists as a created thing, against innovators who say it has not yet been created; Qurtubi names the judge Mundhir ibn Saʿīd al-Balūṭī as falling into that view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r9.anchor: وفيه دليل على ما يقوله أهل الحق من أن النار موجودة مخلوقة خلافا للمبتدعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r10.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r10.claim: Muslim transmits Ibn Masud’s report that the Prophet heard a stone fall into the Fire, where it had been descending for seventy years, and it had just reached the bottom.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r10.anchor: روى مسلم عن عبدالله بن مسعود " قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ سمع وجبة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r11.claim: Bukhari, with a parallel report from Muslim, relates that Paradise and the Fire each stated whom they receive; God says the Fire is His punishment for whom He wills, Paradise His mercy for whom He wills, and each will be filled.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#3/r11.anchor: وروى البخاري عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " احتجت النار والجنة فقالت هذه يدخلني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r1.claim: احتجت can mean تحتج, consistent with Ibn Masud’s stone report; the Prophet was shown the Fire and Paradise during the eclipse prayer and the Night Journey and entered Paradise, so contrary claims are baseless.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r1.anchor: يقال: احتجت بمعنى تحتج للحديث المتقدم حديث ابن مسعود، ولأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أريهما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r2.claim: أعدت may be a circumstantial clause describing the Fire as prepared, with an implied قد because a past verb needs قد in this use; on this parsing, one does not pause at الحجارة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, أعدت may begin a sentence disconnected from what precedes, as in the cited example from 41:23.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كلاما منقطعا عما قبله كما قال: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r4.speaker: السجستاني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r4.claim: Al-Sijistānī makes أعدت للكافرين a second relative clause attached to التي.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r4.anchor: وقال السجستاني: { أعدت للكافرين } من صلة «التي»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī rejects al-Sijistānī’s parsing: التي already has وقودها as its relative clause, whereas in 3:131 أعدت is the only clause attached to التي.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:24#4/r5.anchor: ابن الأنباري: وهذا غلط لأن التي في سورة البقرة قد وصلت بقوله: { وقودها الناس } فلا يجوز

QASHANI:2:24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r1.claim: If they cannot meet the challenge, they should submit, believe, and abandon the obstinacy that leads to the Fire.
QASHANI:2:24/r1.anchor: فاذعنوا وأسلموا وآمنوا، واتركوا العناد المفضي بكم إلى النار

QASHANI:2:24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r2.claim: The omitted necessary response is faith or Islam; avoiding the Fire stands in its place, making denial's punishment explicit.
QASHANI:2:24/r2.anchor: فحذف الملزوم الذي هو الإيمان أو الإسلام، وأقام لازمه الذي هو اتقاء النار مقامه

QASHANI:2:24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r3.claim: The prediction that they will never meet the challenge is an unseen report, since veiled minds cannot produce its like.
QASHANI:2:24/r3.anchor: اعتراض على طريق الإخبار بالغيب للعلم بامتناع عقول المحجوبين عن مثله

QASHANI:2:24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r4.claim: The Fire is the souls' burning turmoil and lower nature, cut off from holy spirit, merciful savor, certainty, and peace while still longing for bodily pleasures and familiar attachments.
QASHANI:2:24/r4.anchor: احتراقهم بثورة نفوسهم، وشرر طباعهم المصروفة عن الروح القدسي الروحاني، والنسيم الذوقي الرحماني،

QASHANI:2:24/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r5.claim: Its fuel is the harsh, lower, inert things people loved; their forms root in the soul and imprison it through attachment.
QASHANI:2:24/r5.anchor: الأمور الجاسية، السفلية، الصامتة، التي تعلقوا بها بالمحبة فرسخت صورتها في أنفسهم،

QASHANI:2:24/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:2:24/r6.claim: The Prophet says a person is gathered with what he loves, even if one loves a stone and is gathered with it.
QASHANI:2:24/r6.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QASHANI:2:24/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r7.claim: Love embeds the beloved's image in the self until it becomes the heart's own image; the Fire's heat follows its spiritual species and kingdom, not merely its body.
QASHANI:2:24/r7.anchor: وقد ركزت صورته في نفسه بالمحبة بحيث صار صورة قلبه صورته.

QASHANI:2:24/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r8.claim: Spiritual fire descends through levels; anger can burn moral character more than fire burns wood, so warmth does not always mean heat.
QASHANI:2:24/r8.anchor: وتلك الروحانية شرر من نار، قهر الله المعنوية بعد تنزلها في مراتب كثيرة

QASHANI:2:24/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r9.claim: Physical fire derives from spiritual fire, making Hell's pain more intense and lasting; bodily powers are finite and weaker than spiritual powers.
QASHANI:2:24/r9.anchor: إذا كانت النار الجسمانية أثرا للنار الروحانية، فلا جرم أن إيلامها أشد وأدوم

QASHANI:2:24/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r10.claim: He reports the saying that Hellfire was washed with water seventy times before being sent down to the world for use.
QASHANI:2:24/r10.anchor: يقال: إن نار جهنم غسلت بالماء سبعين مرة، ثم أنزلت

QASHANI:2:24/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:24/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:24/r11.claim: The disbelievers are those veiled from religion and cut off from attaining what they seek.
QASHANI:2:24/r11.anchor: المحجوبين عن الدين لانقطاعهم دون مرادهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r1.claim: Arab hostility and zeal to discredit Muhammad mean they would have produced a match if able; the added taunt that they will never do so makes their failure proof of the miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r1.anchor: فحيث ما أتوا به ظهر المعجز

RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r2.claim: Muhammad was known for judgment and foresight; if he suspected they could answer, he would not have risked such an emphatic challenge and public disgrace.
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r2.anchor: فلولا معرفته بالاضطرار من حالهم أنهم عاجزون عن المعارضة لما جوز من نفسه أن يحملهم على المعارضة بأبلغ الطرق

RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r3.claim: His certainty that they would never produce a match supports his certainty in his prophethood, since a false claimant would not risk a prediction whose failure exposed him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r3.anchor: فلما جزم دل على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان قاطعا في أمره

RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r4.claim: From Muhammad’s time to Rāzī’s own era, enemies with strong motives to attack Islam never produced a counterexample; this fulfilled prediction is miraculous.
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r4.anchor: ثم إنه مع هذا الحرص الشديد لم توجد المعارضة قط

RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r5.claim: Rāzī concludes these four proofs are contained in the verse, rejecting those who claim the Qur’an offers no evidence or argument.
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r5.anchor: فهذه الوجوه الأربعة في الدلالة على المعجز مما تشتمل عليها هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r6.claim: The conditional “if” follows the opponents’ own assumption: despite their confidence in eloquence, they had not yet accepted that they were unable to answer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p111/r6.anchor: أن يساق القول معهم على حسب حسبانهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r1.claim: A second explanation for “if” is mockery: a confident victor may say “if I defeat you” while knowing defeat is certain.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r1.anchor: أن يتهكم بهم كما يقول الموصوف بالقوة الواثق من نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r2.claim: “If you do not” is shorter than repeating “if you do not bring a sura like it.”
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r2.anchor: لأن هذا أخصر من أن يقال فإن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله ولن تأتوا بسورة من مثله

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r3.claim: ولن تفعلوا is a parenthetical clause and has no syntactic position.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r3.anchor: لا محل لها لأنها جملة اعتراضية

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r4.claim: Lā and lan both negate the future, but lan strengthens the negation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r4.anchor: لا ولن أختان في نفي المستقبل إلا أن في ( لن ) توكيدا وتشديدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r5.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r5.claim: One reported etymology says lan originated as lā plus an.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r5.anchor: أصله لا أن ، وهو قول الخليل

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r6.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says lan is lā with its alif replaced by nūn.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r6.anchor: لا ، أبدلت ألفها نونا ، وهو قول الفراء

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r7.speaker: سيبويه وإحدى الروايتين عن الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r7.claim: Sībawayh and one report from al-Khalīl treat lan as a subjunctive particle that emphasizes future negation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r7.anchor: حرف نصب لتأكيد نفي المستقبل وهو قول سيبويه

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r8.claim: Failure to imitate establishes Muhammad’s truth; persistence in defiance merits punishment, so “guard against the Fire” stands for “abandon stubbornness,” a concise expression that intensifies the threat.

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r9.claim: Waqūd means what a fire is kindled with; as a verbal noun it is usually pronounced with ḍamma, though fatḥ is also attested.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r9.anchor: هو ما يوقد به النار وأما المصدر فمضوم وقد جاء فيه الفتح

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r10.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r10.claim: Sībawayh reports Arabs saying “we kindled the fire with a high flame”; he says the fuel noun is the more common form and can mean firewood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r10.anchor: قال سيبويه : وسمعنا من العرب من يقول

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r11.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r11.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads waqūd with ḍamma, treating it as a verbal noun, like fakhr or zayn.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r11.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بالضم تسمية بالمصدر كما يقال فلان فخر قومه وزين بلده

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r12.claim: People could know that the afterlife fire is fueled by people and stones from earlier teaching by People of the Book, the Prophet, or the earlier verse in al-Taḥrīm.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r12.anchor: لا يمنع أن يتقدم لهم بذلك سماع من أهل الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r13.claim: Al-Taḥrīm 66:6 calls it an indefinite fire because it was revealed in Mecca; al-Baqara uses the definite fire in Medina, referring to what they had already learned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r13.anchor: فعرفوا منها نارا موصوفة بهذه الصفة ثم نزلت هذه بالمدينة مستندة إلى ما عرفوه أولا

RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r14.claim: This fire is distinguished because it burns directly from the people and stones it consumes, unlike ordinary fires first kindled with fuel; its extreme heat also ignites stone.
RAZI-FULL:v2p112/r14.anchor: أن سائر النيران إذا أريد إحراق الناس بها أو إجماء الحجارة أوقدت أولا بوقود

QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r1.claim: Their inability to produce a comparable revelation was certain and proved true; they should beware the shirk that earns the Fire.
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r1.anchor: وأخبر أنهم قطعا لا يقدرون على ذلك ولا يفعلون

QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r2.claim: The Fire is so fierce that even hard stones cannot endure it; frail people have still less capacity to bear it.
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r2.anchor: فإذا كانت تلك النار التي لا تثبت لها الحجارة مع صلابتها

QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r3.claim: After the believers fear the Fire, its being prepared for disbelievers reassures them; God warns His enemies while giving glad tidings to His friends.
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r3.anchor: أعدت للكافرين } ففي ذلك بشارة للمؤمنين . وهذه سنة من الحق سبحانه

QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r4.claim: False claimants' rebukes recoil into hearts, whereas the truthful person's meaning exerts a conquering force upon hearts; distinguishing these effects is difficult.
QUSHAYRI:v1p29/r4.anchor: وأمارة المبطل في دعواه رجوع الزجر منه إلى القلوب ، وعلامة الصادق في معناه

STUDYQURAN:2:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:24/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:24/r1.claim: The stones fueling the Fire are usually understood as sulfur or the idols worshipped by polytheists.
STUDYQURAN:2:24/r1.anchor: The stones are usually taken to be sulfur or the idols (2:22) worshipped by the polytheists (IK

STUDYQURAN:2:24/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:24/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:24/r2.claim: The conditional construction expresses certainty, not uncertainty or contingency, just as laʿalla does not express divine anxiety.
STUDYQURAN:2:24/r2.anchor: conditional if is not an expression of uncertainty in the case of

TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r1.claim: If the opponents cannot produce a surah like the Qur'an after testing themselves and their helpers, their inability proves its divine source, yet they persist in denial.
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r1.anchor: إن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله

TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r2.claim: They will never be able to produce a surah like the Qur'an.
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r2.anchor: أي لن تأتوا بسورة من مثله أبدا

TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the challengers should summon their supporters to attest whether their attempted surah matches the Qur'an.
TAB-FULL:v1p402#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج: «شهداءكم عليها إذا أتيتم بها أنها مثله مثل القرآن»

TAB-FULL:v1p402#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p402#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p402#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that if they cannot meet the challenge, the truth has already been made clear to them.
TAB-FULL:v1p402#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا} [البقرة: 24] فقد بين لكم الحق "

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r1.claim: They must avoid entering the Fire by denying the Messenger's revelation after proof has shown it to be God's revelation and shown their inability to match it.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r1.anchor: بأنه كلامي ووحيي، بعجزكم وعجز جميع خلقي

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r2.claim: With an open wāw, waqūd is a noun meaning fuel like firewood; with a damma, wuqūd is the verbal noun for a fire burning.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r2.anchor: والعرب تجعله مصدرا، وهو اسم إذا فتحت الواو

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r3.claim: The stones are sulfur, which is among the hottest kinds of stone when heated, explaining why it is named as fuel alongside people.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r3.anchor: إنها حجارة الكبريت، وهي أشد الحجارة فيما بلغنا حرا إذا أحميت

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r4.claim: Abdullah reports that the stones are sulfur created in the lowest heaven when God created the heavens and earth, prepared for unbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله، في قوله: " {وقودها الناس والحجارة} [البقرة: 24] قال: هي حجارة من كبريت خلقها الله

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God made the sulfur stones as He willed.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r5.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون، عن ابن مسعود، في قوله: " {وقودها الناس والحجارة} [البقرة: 24] قال: حجارة الكبريت جعلها الله كما شاء

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r6.claim: A report through Ibn Masud and a group of the Prophet's Companions identifies the stones as black sulfur in the Fire, used to punish its people alongside the fire.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r6.anchor: عن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the stones are black sulfur stones in the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج، " في قوله: {وقودها الناس والحجارة} [البقرة: 24] قال: حجارة من كبريت أسود في النار.

TAB-FULL:v1p403/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r8.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r8.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says the stones are harder and larger than the stones people know.
TAB-FULL:v1p403/r8.anchor: وقال لي عمرو بن دينار: حجارة أصلب من هذه وأعظم

TAB-FULL:v1p404/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p404/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p404/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God created sulfur stones with Him as He willed.
TAB-FULL:v1p404/r1.anchor: حجارة من الكبريت خلقها الله عنده كيف شاء

TAB-FULL:v1p405/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p405/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p405/r1.claim: The Fire is prepared for those who deny God as their sole Lord and Creator, despite His provision of the earth and sustenance, and who associate partners with Him in worship.
TAB-FULL:v1p405/r1.anchor: المشركين معه في عبادته الأنداد والآلهة

TAB-FULL:v1p405/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p405/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p405/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning applies to whoever holds the same disbelief as the people addressed.
TAB-FULL:v1p405/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أعدت للكافرين} [البقرة: 24] أي لمن كان على مثل ما أنتم عليه من الكفر "

TABATABAI:2:24-25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r1.claim: Assessing the matter through a discipline outside the researcher's expertise would be overreach, like a linguist trying to prove or disprove an astronomical claim from linguistics.
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r1.anchor: نظير ما لو أراد الباحث في علم اللغة أن يستظهر من علمه حكم الفلك نفيا أو إثباتا

TABATABAI:2:24-25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r3.claim: People are both fuel for the Fire and those consumed by it: each is punished by a fire kindled by that person's own deeds.
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r3.anchor: وقد نصت الآية على أنه نفس الإنسان، فالإنسان وقود وموقود عليه

TABATABAI:2:24-25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r6.claim: The stones used as fuel are the idols people worshipped, as supported by the statement that worshippers and what they worship are fuel for Hell.
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r6.anchor: والمراد بالحجارة في قوله { وقودها الناس والحجارة } ، الأصنام التي كانوا يعبدونها

TABATABAI:2:24-25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:24-25/r7.claim: The word ḥaṣab in the supporting verse means fuel.

AKHFASH:v1p56#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p56#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p56#2/r1.claim: Al-waqūd can mean the firewood that fuels the fire, or the act of kindling.

AKHFASH:v1p56#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p56#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p56#2/r2.claim: The two vocalizations distinguish fuel from burning, though some regard them as dialect forms with the same meaning.

TABRISI:2:24/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r1.claim: إن is conditional; لم negates the present verb with past sense and makes it jussive, with the plural nun omitted.
TABRISI:2:24/r1.anchor: إن حرف شرط و لم حرف يدخل على الفعل المضارع فينفيه ويجعله بمعنى الماضي ويعمل فيه الجزم

TABRISI:2:24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r2.claim: لن negates the present verb for the future and makes it subjunctive; the plural nun is omitted.
TABRISI:2:24/r2.anchor: ولن يدخل على الفعل المضارع فيخصه بالاستقبال وينفيه ويعمل فيه النصب وعلامة النصب

TABRISI:2:24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r3.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:2:24/r3.claim: Al-Khalil says لن contracts لا أن through frequent use, like ويلمه and هلا, and is treated as one particle.
TABRISI:2:24/r3.anchor: زعم الخليل أنها لا أن ولكنهم حذفوا لكثرته في كلامهم كما قالوا ويلمه

TABRISI:2:24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:24/r4.claim: Sibawayh rejects the derivation from لا أن because it would bar object-fronting before لن, although grammarians allow such fronting.
TABRISI:2:24/r4.anchor: قال وهذا ليس بجيد لأنه لو كان كذلك لم يجز زيدا لن أضرب

TABRISI:2:24/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r5.claim: ولن تفعلوا has no syntactic position; it is a parenthesis between the condition and its apodosis.
TABRISI:2:24/r5.anchor: لا موضع له من الإعراب لأنه اعتراض وقع بين الشرط والجزاء

TABRISI:2:24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r6.claim: If they cannot produce a comparable sura despite their allies and helpers, and recognize the creation's inability, they must stop denying the Quran.
TABRISI:2:24/r6.anchor: وقد تظاهرتم أنتم وشركاؤكم عليه وأعوانكم وتبين لكم عجزكم وعجز جميع الخلق عنه

TABRISI:2:24/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r7.claim: The prediction that they will never produce its like is an enduring future denial and proves Muhammad's prophethood because events confirmed it.
TABRISI:2:24/r7.anchor: لأن لن تنفي على التأبيد في المستقبل وفيه دلالة على صحة نبوة نبينا محمد

TABRISI:2:24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r8.claim: Fear the Fire by avoiding denial; this duty follows once the miracle establishes prophethood, since only then is punishment known.
TABRISI:2:24/r8.anchor: لا يلزمهم الإتقاء إلا بعد التصديق بالنبوة ولا يصح العلم بالنبوة إلا بعد قيام المعجزة

TABRISI:2:24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24/r9.claim: The people and stones are the Fire's fuel; the stones most likely mean carved idols worshipped beside God, as in 21:98.
TABRISI:2:24/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن الناس والحجارة وقود النار أي حطبها يريد بها أصنامهم المنحوتة من الحجارة

TABRISI:2:24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
TABRISI:2:24/r10.claim: One view identifies the stones as sulfur, which burns especially fiercely when heated.
TABRISI:2:24/r10.anchor: إنها أحر شيء إذا أحميت عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس

TABRISI:2:24#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r1.claim: The idol interpretation is supported by 21:98, which calls the objects worshipped besides God the fuel of Hell.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r1.anchor: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم

TABRISI:2:24#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r2.claim: Mention of stones conveys the Fire's terrible magnitude: a Fire that consumes stones must be terrifying.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r2.anchor: وقيل ذكر الحجارة دليل على عظم تلك النار لأنها لا تأكل الحجارة إلا وهي في غاية الفظاعة والهول

TABRISI:2:24#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r3.claim: Another view says God preserves sinners' bodies on the Fire as fuel stones endure; the renewal of their skins supports this, 4:56.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه إن أجسادهم تبقى على النار بقاء الحجارة التي توقد بها النار بتبقية الله إياها

TABRISI:2:24#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r4.claim: A further view takes the stones as heated rocks with which sinners are tortured.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه إنهم يعذبون بالحجارة المحمية بالنار

TABRISI:2:24#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r5.claim: The Fire is made ready for disbelievers because they remain there forever and make up most of its inhabitants.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r5.anchor: خلقت وهيئت للكافرين لأنهم الذين يخلدون فيها ولأنهم أكثر أهل النار

TABRISI:2:24#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r6.claim: Another view takes this as a Fire reserved for disbelievers, though sinners also have a Fire; compare the hypocrites' lowest level in 4:145.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r6.anchor: وقيل إنما خص النار بكونها معدة للكافرين وإن كانت معدة للفاسقين أيضا

TABRISI:2:24#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r7.claim: The verse validates rational argument: if the Quran were human speech, skilled opponents could match it; their failure shows it is divine.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على بطلان قول من حرم النظر والحجاج العقلي

TABRISI:2:24#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:24#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:24#2/r8.claim: Prepared things already exist, so the Fire is created now; the same applies to Paradise prepared for the godfearing, which angels can witness.
TABRISI:2:24#2/r8.anchor: لأن المعد لا يكون إلا موجودا وكذلك الجنة

FARRA:v1p19/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p19/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p19/r3.claim: People and stones both serve as the fire’s fuel.

FARRA:v1p19/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p19/r4.speaker: زعموا
FARRA:v1p19/r4.claim: Some say the stones are sulfur, which becomes intensely hot and is the hottest stone when heated.

FARRA:v1p19/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p19/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p19/r5.claim: The fire has been prepared for the unbelievers.
FARRA:v1p19/r5.anchor: ثم قال: أعدت للكافرين يعنى النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r1.claim: Lam jussives a present-tense verb while giving it past sense; after a conditional particle a past verb can mean the future, making lam resemble conditional particles.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r1.anchor: (لم) حرف يجزم الفعل المضارع، ويقع بعدها بمعنى الماضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r2.claim: Conditional particles govern jussive forms because they call for two clauses; the long construction favors deletion and lightening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r2.anchor: لأنها تقتضي جملتين كقولك: (إن تضرب أضرب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r3.claim: Lan is an independent particle for future negation, governing its verb in the subjunctive like an; it is not a relative particle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r3.anchor: فهي حرف قائم بنفسه، وضع لنفس الفعل المستقبل، ونصبه للفعل كنصب (أن)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r4.claim: Lan yafal denies sayafalu, and the verb after lan can govern an object placed before it, evidence that lan is independent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r4.anchor: نفى سيفعل، وتعمل ما بعدها فيما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r5.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r5.claim: Al-Khalil proposes that lan originated as la an, with the two particles contracted for ease of pronunciation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r5.anchor: وروى سيبويه عن بعض أصحاب الخليل عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r6.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r6.claim: Sibawayh calls al-Khalil’s derivation unsound: if lan contained an, an object could not precede it because that would place a relative clause before its antecedent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r6.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن هذا ليس بجيد، ولو كان كذلك لم يجز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r7.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r7.claim: Al-Khalil answers that compounded particles can behave differently from their parts; adding la to hal permits an object before halla.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r7.anchor: وللخليل أن ينفصل من هذا بأن يقول: الحروف إذا ركبت خرجت عما كانت عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r8.claim: The author finds al-Khalil’s derivation weak: when a form’s apparent meaning works, one should not posit another origin without decisive proof or necessity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r8.anchor: وجه آخر، وهو أن اللفظ متى جاء على صيغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r9.claim: The challenge means: if you failed to do it in the past, you will never do it in the future.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p252/r9.anchor: ومعنى الآية: فإن لم تفعلوا فيما مضى، ولن تفعلوا فيما يستقبل أبدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r1.claim: The statement ‘you will never do it’ is parenthetical between the conditional clause and its answer; parentheticals also occur between subject and predicate or between inna’s noun and predicate.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r2.claim: They are commanded to beware of entering the Fire through their denial, after proof of God’s oneness and Muhammad’s truth had been established against them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r2.anchor: أي: فاحذروا أن تصلوا النار بتكذيبكم، وإنما قيل لهم هذا بعد أن ثبتت الحجة عليهم في التوحيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r3.claim: The fa in fa-in is coordinative, while the fa in fattaqu is for following or consequence rather than coordination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r3.anchor: و (الفاء) في قوله: {فإن لم} للعطف، وفي قوله: {فاتقوا} للإتباع دون العطف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r4.claim: Fa introduces a conditional answer when the answer is a full independent clause, including nominal, imperative, or prohibitive clauses; it connects the condition to an answer that otherwise could stand alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p254/r4.anchor: اختاروا (الفاء) من قبل أن الجزاء سبيله أن يقع ثاني الشرط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r1.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says waqud with ḍamma is the verbal noun of waqada, ‘the fire burned’; the word can also describe good firewood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r1.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: (الوقود) بالضم، المصدر يقال: وقدت النار، تقد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r2.claim: Other linguists allow both vowelings: ḍamma is the verbal noun, while fatḥa is a noun, though fatḥa may also be a verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r2.anchor: وكأن الوقود اسم وضع موضع المصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r3.claim: The plural ḥijāra is irregular for ḥajar; the regular analogical plural is aḥjār, like other nonstandard plural patterns cited here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r3.anchor: و (الحجارة) جمع حجر، وليس بقياس، ولكنهم قالوه كما قالوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes identify the stones as sulfur stones, which burn more fiercely.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r4.anchor: الحجارة هاهنا: حجارة الكبريت، عن ابن عباس وغيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r5.claim: Mentioning stones signals the Fire’s enormity: a fire that consumes stones must be terrifying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r5.anchor: وقيل: ذكر الحجارة دليل على عظم تلك النار، لأنها لا تأكل الحجارة إلا كانت فظيعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r6.claim: Calling people the Fire’s fuel does not mean it is not yet created: it already burns without them and they become its fuel when they enter; ‘prepared’ also shows it exists, since the nonexistent is not prepared.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r6.anchor: على أنها غير مخلوقة بأن الناس لم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r7.claim: The Fire is described as prepared for disbelievers although sinful Muslims enter it, because disbelievers remain forever while believers’ stay is brief by comparison; it is not said to be prepared for the addressed people because some will believe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r7.anchor: يدخلونها، لأن الكافرين يخلدون فيها دون المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r8.claim: After mentioning the disbelievers’ punishment for denial, the passage turns to the believers’ reward for belief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p256/r8.anchor: ذكر جزاء المؤمنين لتصديقهم فقال عز من قائل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r1.claim: With fatḥa on the wāw, waqūd means firewood or fuel.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r1.anchor: أي حطبها. والوقود: الحطب؛ بفتح الواو.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r2.claim: With ḍamma on the wāw, wuqūd means the act of burning or kindling.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r2.anchor: الوقود: الحطب؛ بفتح الواو. والوقود بضمها: توقدها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p43#3/r3.claim: The commentators identify the stones as stones of sulfur.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r1.claim: The challenge extends into the future: they will never produce what is demanded, so they must beware the Fire.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r2.claim: To fear the Fire is to guard against reaching it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r2.anchor: فاحذروا أن تصلوا { النار التي وقودها } ما يوقد به

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r3.claim: The stones serving as fuel are sulfur stones, which catch fire especially intensely.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r3.anchor: يعني حجارة الكبريت، وهي أشد لاتقادها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:24-25/r4.claim: The Fire was created and prepared as recompense for those who disbelieve by denial.

ELMALILI:2:23-24/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24/r7.claim: They cannot meet the challenge at any time through the Resurrection; even if it were possible in principle, God will not enable them to do so.
ELMALILI:2:23-24/r7.anchor: Yapmanız mümkin değil ya, mümkin olsa da yapamayacaksınız, Allah yaptırmayacak

ELMALILI:2:23-24/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24/r8.claim: The failure warning leads to the dreadful Fire, whose fuel is people and stones and which has been prepared for disbelievers.
ELMALILI:2:23-24/r8.anchor: bu ateş, bu nâr-ı cahîm, kâfirler için hazırlanmıştır

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r1.claim: Certainty rests on direct perception, rational inference, experience, and report; some recognize the Qur’an’s elevated composition directly, while others learn of it from those who do.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r1.anchor: Bedâhet, şuhûd, istidlâl-i aklî, tecribe, haber, bunlar ilmin, yakīnin en mühim vâsıtaları, mi‘yarlarıdır

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r2.claim: Revelation itself cannot be experimentally repeated because it is a unique divine event, but its effects can be tested; the challenge supplies a special measure whose result can be confirmed across generations.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r2.anchor: Gerçi siz vahyi bizzat tecribe edemezsiniz

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r3.claim: Testing an effect can reveal whether its cause is general or unique, just as people infer the sun from its light; testing all revelations directly would outlast a lifetime.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r3.anchor: Güneşin doğduğunu ziyâsından anlarsınız. Böyle bir tecribe size sebeb-i vâki‘in küllî ve umûmî mi, yoksa münferid ve mümtaz bir şey mi olduğunu anlatır

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r4.claim: The challenge leaves opponents free to try and does not restrain them by force; its categorical forecast and ensuing failure make it an unusually decisive proof of revelation’s inimitability.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r4.anchor: Sizi bir mütegallibin kuvve-i cebriyesiyle bağlamıyor, ikinizi bir yere getirmekten men‘etmiyor. Hür, muhtâr, serbest bırakıyor

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r5.claim: Even if critics attribute the Qur’an to Muhammad’s uniquely gifted nature, they should trust his testimony: he calls himself God’s servant and Messenger, seeks no worldly dominion, and asks no wage beyond affection for kin.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r5.anchor: kemâl-i tevâzu‘ile “ben Allah’ın bir kulu ve Resûlüyüm” diyor ve sonra kemâl-i yakīn ile وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا۟ diyor

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r6.claim: A person who doubts God should believe on the testimony of such an exceptional mind; a believer has even stronger reason to accept that God sent the revelation to disclose Himself and His commands.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r6.anchor: Eğer Allah’a inanmıyorsanız, O’nda şüpheniz varsa böyle bir aklın şehâdetiyle O’na inanmanız

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r7.claim: Once rational, experiential, and scientific grounds for doubt fail, continued suspicion can only arise from obstinacy, self-interest, or immorality; unjustified doubters, like outright deniers, are disbelievers without excuse.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r7.anchor: Bunu bilmez, hâlâ şüphe davasından vazgeçmez, hâlâ kuşkulanırsanız buna inadınızdan, ağrâz-ı şahsiyenizden, ahlâksızlığınızdan başka bir sebep kalmaz

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r8.claim: The prediction has been vindicated over 1,344 years: despite rivalry, arms, bloodshed, upheaval, and great expense, no refuting answer was produced; opponents resorted to diversion, while divine justice and the Fire remain.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r8.anchor: Kur’ân’ın işbu وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا۟ ihbârı o günden bugüne kadar bin üç yüz kırk dört senelik bir tecribe ile sıdkını gösteren bir mu‘cize-i ebediyedir

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r9.claim: Elmalılı says the stones can refer to the idols and structures worshipped, which help kindle the Fire alongside the people who worshipped them.

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r10.claim: He also reads the wording as indicating combustible stones such as coal; waqūd can denote any kindling or fuel, including grass, tinder, rags, and wood.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r10.anchor: “Vekūd”, ateş yakılan kibrit, ot, çöp, çıra, paçavra

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r11.speaker: erbâb-ı fen
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r11.claim: Elmalılı reports that experts in the sciences identify the combustible stones as coal.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r11.anchor: erbâb-ı fen bunun taş kömürler olduğunu söylüyorlar

ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r12.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquent address shifts focus among a broad audience, particular groups, opponents, allies, and the Prophet’s special servant, moving from a public warning to a more intimate address.
ELMALILI:2:23-24#2/r12.anchor: nihâyet acı bir inzar ile tamam oldu, derken gülüyor, bir hususiyet daha alıyor

MAJAZ:v1p34/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p34/r1.claim: He glosses waqūd as the people and stones serving as fuel, and says with initial ḍamma it denotes burning.
MAJAZ:v1p34/r1.anchor: «وقودها الناس والحجارة» (24) : حطبها الناس، والوقود مضموم الأول التلهب.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r1.claim: The fire in the verse is the fire of Hell, whose fuel is people and stones.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r2.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r2.claim: Some commentators take the stones to mean stone statues and idols worshipped as gods.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r2.anchor: Bazı müfessirler bu taştan maksadın tapınılan taş heykeller, tanrı timsalleri olduğunu düşünmüşlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r3.claim: Because punishing inanimate objects would be unjust and unreasonable, he prefers people as conscious, willing creatures and stones as unseen entities of unknown nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r3.anchor: taş yakıtı ise “gayb âlemine ait, mahiyeti dünyalılar tarafından bilinemeyen bir nesne” olarak yorumlamak daha uygundur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r4.speaker: hadisler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r4.claim: Hadiths state that Hell's fire is seventy times more intense in its burning than earthly fire; the commentary cites Bukhari and Tirmidhi collections.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r4.anchor: Hadislere göre cehennem ateşi, yakıcılık bakımından dünya ateşinden yetmiş misli daha şiddetlidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r5.claim: Since lasers cut diamonds today, stones may also separate and burn in fires whose nature and intensity are unknown to us.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r5.anchor: Bugün lazerle elmas kesiliyor. Mahiyet ve şiddetini bilmediğimiz ateşlerle taşların da ayrışıp yanması mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r6.claim: The thought of a delicate human body suffering in such a fire without dying or being consumed is horrifying.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r6.anchor: İnsan vücudu gibi narin bir cismin böyle bir ateşte ölmeden ve tükenmeden azap görmesinin tasavvuru bile dehşet vericidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r7.claim: The Qur'an was sent to protect people from this fire and call them to mercy, Paradise, and eternal bliss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:24/r7.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm insanları işte bu ateşten korumak için gönderilmiştir ve onları rahmete, cennete, ebedî saadete çağırmaktadır.

NAHHAS:v1p199/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r10.claim: Here «إن» does not govern in the written form, so it can precede «لم» as it can a past verb; the phrase means “if you leave the act undone.”
NAHHAS:v1p199/r10.anchor: فمعنى إن لم تفعلوا إن تركتم الفعل

NAHHAS:v1p199/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r11.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v1p199/r11.claim: Al-Akhfash says «لم» makes the verb jussive because it is a negation like «لا» in «لا رجل في الدار», removing the ending vowel as tanwin is removed from nouns.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r11.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد إنما جزموا بلم لأنها نفي فأشبهت لا

NAHHAS:v1p199/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r12.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v1p199/r12.claim: Other grammarians say «لم» governs jussive because, like the conditional «إن», it turns the future to past and requires a response; verbs therefore lose their ending vowel.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r12.anchor: وقال غيره جزمت بها لأنها أشبهت إن التي للشرط لأنها ترد المستقبل إلى الماضي

NAHHAS:v1p199/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r13.claim: «لن» makes the verb subjunctive, marked by dropping its nūn; subjunctive and jussive are parallel secondary cases, as accusative and genitive are for nouns.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r13.anchor: نصب بلن وعلامة نصبه حذف النون واستوى النصب والجزم في الأفعال

NAHHAS:v1p199/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r14.speaker: الخليل
NAHHAS:v1p199/r14.claim: Al-Khalīl is reported to derive «لن» from «لا أن».
NAHHAS:v1p199/r14.anchor: وحكي عن الخليل رحمه الله أن أصل لن لا أن

NAHHAS:v1p199/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r15.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p199/r15.claim: Sībawayh objects to deriving «لن» from «لا أن», arguing that this would make «زيدا لن أضرب» impermissible.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r15.anchor: ورد عليه هذا سيبويه وقال لو كان كذا لما جاز زيدا لن أضرب

NAHHAS:v1p199/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r16.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v1p199/r16.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says some Arabs make «لن» jussive, as they do «لم».
NAHHAS:v1p199/r16.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة من العرب من يجزم بلن كما يجزم بلم

NAHHAS:v1p199/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r17.claim: The response to the condition is «فاتقوا النار» and what follows it.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r17.anchor: ( فاتقوا النار ) جواب الشرط في الفاء وما بعدها

NAHHAS:v1p199/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r18.claim: Tamīm and Asad have the dialect form «فتقوا النار».

NAHHAS:v1p199/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r19.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p199/r19.claim: Sībawayh cites the verb pair «تقى يتقي» for the form.

NAHHAS:v1p199/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r22.claim: «وقودها» is the subject and «الناس» its predicate, with «الحجارة» coordinated to «الناس».
NAHHAS:v1p199/r22.anchor: ( وقودها ) مبتدأ ( الناس ) خبر ( والحجارة ) عطف عليهم

NAHHAS:v1p199/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r23.claim: Basrans treat the feminine tāʾ as silent because it is a grammatical particle.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r23.anchor: أسكنت عند البصريين لأنها حرف جاء لمعنى

NAHHAS:v1p199/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r24.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p199/r24.claim: The Kufans explain the remaining feminine tāʾ as itself serving as the sign after the other marked tāʾ forms were distinguished by their vowels.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r24.anchor: وعند الكوفيين إنك لما ضممت تاء المخاطب وفتحت تاء المخاطب المذكر

NAHHAS:v1p199/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r25.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r25.claim: The passive subject in «أعدت» is an unexpressed pronoun.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r25.anchor: واسم ما لم يسم فاعله مضمر في أعدت

NAHHAS:v1p199/r26.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r26.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r26.claim: The lām before «الكافرين» is an added preposition, and the noun is genitive after it.

NAHHAS:v1p199/r27.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r27.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف
NAHHAS:v1p199/r27.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujāhid, and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «التي وقودها» with a ḍamma on the wāw of «وقود».
NAHHAS:v1p199/r27.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وطلحة بن مصرف ( التي وقودها ) بضم الواو

NAHHAS:v1p199/r28.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r28.speaker: الكسائي والأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v1p199/r28.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash distinguish «وَقود» with fatḥa as fuel from «وُقود» with ḍamma as the act of burning.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r28.anchor: وقال الكسائي والأخفش سعيد الوقود بفتح الواو الحطب والوقود بضمها الفعل

NAHHAS:v1p199/r29.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p199/r29.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p199/r29.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says the fuel sense requires the reading with fatḥa, while noting al-Akhfash's report that Arabs use both forms for fuel and verbal noun, with the first more common.
NAHHAS:v1p199/r29.anchor: قال أبو جعفر يجب على هذا أن لا يقرأ إلا وقودها بفتح الواو لأن المعنى حطبها

BURHAN:v1p381#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p381#2/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p381#2/r5.claim: An added alif after plural waw marks the weight of the verbal clause; it remains when a subjunctive or jussive governs the verb, as here.
BURHAN:v1p381#2/r5.anchor: فإن دخل ناصب أو جازم مثل

BURHAN:v2p421/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p421/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p421/r2.claim: Al-Zarkashi concludes that لا and لن simply negate future actions; whether negation is eternal comes from external evidence, not from either particle itself.
BURHAN:v2p421/r2.anchor: والحق ان لا ولن لمجرد النفي عن الافعال المستقبله والتأبيد وعدمه يؤخذان من دليل خارج

BURHAN:v2p421/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p421/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p421/r3.claim: Claims that لن inherently means perpetual negation fail because the Qur'an limits it by today, adds أبدا after it, and gives it an endpoint in other passages.
BURHAN:v2p421/r3.anchor: ولو كانت للتأبيد لم يقيد منفيها باليوم

BURHAN:v3p175/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p175/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p175/r4.claim: Sometimes a transitive verb is treated as intransitive because only the occurrence of the action matters; no omitted object is intended, and such an object is termed dead.
BURHAN:v3p175/r4.anchor: ألا يكون المفعول مقصودا أصلا وينزل الفعل المتعدي منزلة القاصر

BURHAN:v3p175/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p175/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p175/r5.claim: Not every contextually imaginable object is grammatically omitted: فعلوا, like eat and drink, can refer simply to performing the action rather than an identified object.
BURHAN:v3p175/r5.anchor: وبهذا يعلم أنه ليس كل ما هو لازم من موضوع الكلام مقدرا فيه

BURHAN:v3p232/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p232/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p232/r1.claim: A clause after علم can fill both object positions without ellipsis; in passive syntax the نائب عن الفاعل bears the agent's status and occupies the patient's position.
BURHAN:v3p232/r1.anchor: الجملة سادة مسد المفعولين فإن الجملة محلة لاسم واحد سد مسد اسمين مفعولين من غير حذف

BURHAN:v3p232/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p232/r2.speaker: ابن الأثير
BURHAN:v3p232/r2.claim: Interrogatives and conditionals can compress multiple alternatives or names: كم مالك can mean twenty or thirty, and من يقم can cover Zayd or Amr; universal terms do similar work.

BURHAN:v3p232/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p232/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p232/r3.claim: Plural and dual forms compress repeated names; the dual contains two instances joined without an expressed conjunction, while unlike names are repeated with coordination.
BURHAN:v3p232/r3.anchor: فإن الزيدين يغنى عن زيد وزيد وزيد وكذا التثنية أصلها رجل ورجل

BURHAN:v3p232/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p232/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p232/r4.claim: The verb فعل often stands for multiple deeds; in the challenge here, it means bringing a surah like the Qur'an, which they will never do.
BURHAN:v3p232/r4.anchor: أي فإن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله ولن تأتوا بسورة من مثله

BURHAN:v3p232/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p232/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p232/r5.claim: Fronting and delaying are eloquent techniques that display command of language and have an agreeable effect; the sound view is that they are not metaphor.
BURHAN:v3p232/r5.anchor: والصحيح أنه ليس منه فإن المجاز نقل ما وضع له إلى ما لم يوضع

ITQAN:v2p506/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p506/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p506/r1.claim: لن is a future negation particle governing the subjunctive; al-Zamakhshari and Ibn al-Khabaz say it makes negation more emphatic than لا.
ITQAN:v2p506/r1.anchor: حرف نفي ونصب واستقبال والنفي بها أبلغ من النفي بلا فهي لتأكيد النفي كما ذكره الزمخشري وابن الخباز

ITQAN:v2p506/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p506/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v2p506/r2.claim: One view distinguishes لن as denying “I will do” from لا as denying “I do,” like the distinction made by لم and لما.
ITQAN:v2p506/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم وإن منعه مكابرة فهي لنفي إني أفعل ولا لنفي أفعل كما في لم ولما

ITQAN:v2p506/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p506/r3.speaker: ابن الزملكاني
ITQAN:v2p506/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zamalkani reports that Arabs use لن to deny what is expected and لا to deny what is doubtful.
ITQAN:v2p506/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم العرب تنفي المظنون بلن والمشكوك بلا ذكره ابن الزملكاني في التبيان

ITQAN:v2p506/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p506/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p506/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that لن makes negation permanent, citing the impossibility of creating a fly and the challenge that opponents will never meet.
ITQAN:v2p506/r4.anchor: وادعى الزمخشري أيضا أنها لتأييد النفي

ITQAN:v2p506/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p506/r8.speaker: ابن الزملكاني
ITQAN:v2p506/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zamalkani reverses al-Zamakhshari: لن denies something near in time and does not extend the negation.
ITQAN:v2p506/r8.anchor: وعكس ابن الزملكاني مقالة الزمخشري فقال إن لن لنفي ما قرب وعدم امتداد النفي

RUMMANI:v1p96/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p96/r1.claim: Harmony in articulation is moderation among letter outlets, avoiding extremes of distance or closeness.
RUMMANI:v1p96/r1.anchor: والتلاؤم في التعديل من غير بعد شديد أو قرب شديد

RUMMANI:v1p96/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p96/r2.claim: Harmony is perceived through ease on the tongue, pleasing sound, and acceptance by natural taste.
RUMMANI:v1p96/r2.anchor: يظهر بسهولته على اللسان , وحسنه في الأسماع , وتقبله في الطباع

RUMMANI:v1p96/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p96/r3.claim: When this sound harmony joins the highest clarity and sound proof, the perceptive listener recognizes the Qur'an's inimitability.
RUMMANI:v1p96/r3.anchor: إذا انضاف إلى ذلك حسن البيان في صحة البرهان في أعلى الطبقات ظهر الإعجاز

RUMMANI:v1p96/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p96/r4.claim: The universal challenge and the promise that they will never answer it make incapacity decisive; the author also cites challenges to a Qur'an, a sura, and ten suras as proof that Arabs and non-Arabs cannot match it.
RUMMANI:v1p96/r4.anchor: ثم قال: {فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا} فقطع بأنهم لن يفعلوا

RUMMANI:v1p109/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p109/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p109/r1.claim: The author lists several aspects of inimitability: abandoning an answer despite strong motives, challenging everyone, diversion of intent, eloquence, truthful predictions, breaking customary patterns, and comparison with other miracles.
RUMMANI:v1p109/r1.anchor: وهي: ترك المعارضة مع توفر الدواعي وشدة الحاجة , والتحدي للكافة

RUMMANI:v1p109/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p109/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p109/r2.claim: Strong motives produce action when an act is possible; when people do not respond to the Qur'anic challenge despite strong motives, that failure shows they cannot answer.
RUMMANI:v1p109/r2.anchor: معارضة على القرآن لما لم تقع المعارضة دل ذلك على العجز عنها

RUMMANI:v1p109/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p109/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p109/r3.claim: A challenge addressed to everyone makes it especially clear that people would not leave it unanswered despite strong motives unless they were unable.
RUMMANI:v1p109/r3.anchor: وأما التحدي للكافة فهو أظهر في أنهم لا يجوز أن يتركوا المعارضة

RUMMANI:v1p109/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p109/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
RUMMANI:v1p109/r4.claim: Some scholars explain inimitability through ṣarfah, God's diverting people's intentions from attempting a response.
RUMMANI:v1p109/r4.anchor: وعلى ذلك كان يعتمد بعض أهل العلم في أن القرآن معجز من جهة صرف الهمم

RUMMANI:v1p109/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p109/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p109/r5.claim: Al-Rummani accepts ṣarfah as one aspect of inimitability: it lies outside customary patterns, like the other miracles that attest to prophethood.
RUMMANI:v1p109/r5.anchor: وهذا عندنا أحد وجوه الإعجاز التي يظهر منها للعقول

RUMMANI:v1p109/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p109/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p109/r6.claim: Truthful reports about future events cannot arise by coincidence and therefore come from the Knower of the unseen; examples include Badr, the Romans' recovery, Islam's ascendancy, the challenge's failure, and other predictions.
RUMMANI:v1p109/r6.anchor: وأما الأخبار الصادقة عن الأمور المستقبلة فإنه لما كان لا يجوز أن تقع على الاتفاق دل على أنها من عند علام الغيوب

BURHAN:v2p257/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p257/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p257/r3.claim: A consequence can stand for its cause: fear of Fire means shun defiance, eating orphan property entails Fire, consuming wealth by falsehood means gambling, and al-rijz means idol worship that causes punishment.
BURHAN:v2p257/r3.anchor: ﴿ فاتقوا النار ﴾ أي العناد المستلزم للنار

BURHAN:v2p110/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p110/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p110/r4.claim: The assurance “you will never do so” intensifies the challenge and culminates in a warning to fear the Fire.

BURHAN:v2p110/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p110/r5.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
BURHAN:v2p110/r5.claim: Al-Walīd, one of Quraysh’s leading eloquent men, judged that the Qurʾān was neither poetry, magic, madness, nor soothsaying.
BURHAN:v2p110/r5.anchor: الوليد بن المغيرة لعنه الله كان سيد قريش وأحد فصحائهم لما سمعه

BURHAN:v2p301/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p301/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p301/r6.claim: The warning about Hell’s fuel alludes to not persisting in opposition after the miracle becomes clear, lest the fire seize the opponents.
BURHAN:v2p301/r6.anchor: فانه كناية عن الا تعاندوا عند ظهور المعجزة فتمسكم هذه النار العظيمة

BURHAN:v4p56/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p56/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p56/r3.claim: The conditional إن, normally associated with uncertainty, taunts the opponents by speaking according to their presumed chance of matching the Qur'an, like a confident challenger.
BURHAN:v4p56/r3.anchor: جيئ ب إن التي للشك وهو واجب دون اذ التي للوجوب سوقا للكلام على حسب حسبانهم

BURHAN:v4p215/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p215/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p215/r6.claim: With لم the jussive is attributed to لم, but with لا as in unless You forgive me, the jussive is attributed to إن.
BURHAN:v4p215/r6.anchor: إن دخلت إن على لم يكن الجزم لم لابها

BURHAN:v2p308/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p308/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p308/r7.claim: A concise verb can stand for several actions; in فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا the omitted actions are producing a sura like the Qur’an, which they will never produce.
BURHAN:v2p308/r7.anchor: تاسعها قصد الاختصار ومنه الكناية عن افعال

BURHAN:v2p64/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p64/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p64/r2.claim: The Meccan verse uses an indefinite “fire” because its later description was not yet familiar; the Medinan Baqarah verse uses the definite article for the fire already introduced.
BURHAN:v2p64/r2.anchor: لأنها نزلت بمكة قبل آية البقرة فلم تكن النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة معروفة

ITQAN:v3p129/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p129/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p129/r9.claim: A fifth purpose is brevity, using “do” to stand for many words: “what they used to do” and “if you do not, and never will” mean failing to produce a comparable sura.
ITQAN:v3p129/r9.anchor: خامسها قصد الاختصار كالكناية عن ألفاظ متعددة بلفظ ( فعل ) نحو ﴿ لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون ﴾ ﴿ فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا ﴾ أي فإن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r2.claim: The challenge in al-Baqara to produce a comparable sura, followed by the declaration that they cannot, settles the Qur’an’s inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p178/r2.anchor: وفي هذه السورة المدنية الأولى، حسم القرآن قضية المعاجزة بهذا التحدي الصادع:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p68/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p68/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p68/r3.claim: At the start of the Medinan period, the challenge narrowed to a single sura, concluding the dispute after 87 Meccan suras had left the Arabs unable to match the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p68/r3.anchor: وبعدها، في مستهل العهد المدني نزلت آية البقرة، أولى السور المدنيات، والتحدي فيها بسورة من مثله إنهاء لهذا الجدل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r4.claim: The threat follows the challenge: those who reject after proof has been established and fail to use reason are likened to stones.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p851/r4.anchor: والذي لا يؤمن قامت عليه الحجة ولم يستعمل عقله فيكون بمنزلة الحجارة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p130/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p130/r2.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p130/r2.claim: Abduh locates Quranic inimitability in its striking varied structures, rhythms, and styles, unlike patterns abstracted from Arabic speech; each surah has its own form and effect.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p130/r2.anchor: على نحو ما فعل "الشيخ محمد عبده" في تفسير آيتى البقرة:
